TextEng: <FirstName>? Oh good, you're alive. I'm not sure this place is safe though, but it was the best I could find.
For a moment I thought you wouldn't recover. I hope you're strong enough to continue?
Sir Gilbert Hawklin is pleased to announce a tourney will take place in Thunderstone to seek the greatest knights in the land. The tourney will be held in the fields on the east side of town.

Lord Marvin Huntcrown has publicly announced that he is to give up hunting, and is looking to sell his hounds to the highest bidder. Anyone interested in the finest pedigree boar or deerhounds, should request an appointment with Lord Marvin via his butler.

All citizens of Thunderstone are asked to be especially courteous to Sembian visitors. Repeated allegations of spying have generated an official complaint from the Sembian Envoy in Wheloon. Unfounded allegations are also a waste of the Crown's time.
The Crown is pleased to announce the recent knighting of <CUSTOM1021> <FullName>. The application for the knighthood of Alanis Broadhouse was rejected due to the recent brawl in the Furniture's Fate.

Alanis Broadhouse and <FullName> have recently been recommended as new knights to the Princess Regent in Suzail. Objections should be raised through the normal official channels if any believe these two are not worthy of knighthood.
Jenny Drabb has requested that should anyone see her cat, please report it to the Crown Office. Additionally, Sir Gilbert Hawklin is pleased to announce he has taken on a new squire, <FullName>.
Sir Gilbert Hawklin is pleased to announce a tourney will take place in Thunderstone to seek the greatest knights in the land. The tourney will be held in the fields on the east side of town.
I'm up next. Don't distract me!
They'll be time for talk once I've won the archery competition.
Hush now, I'm watching the competition!
Hello there. Are ya interested in entering the archery competition? Any man or woman with bow or crossbow may enter.
Well come back when you are then. We'll be waitin'.
I don't see enough arrows in your quiver there mate. 18 ya need, unless ya plan to go out of the competition before the end!
Well get ya bow or crossbow out then. Ya can't enter without one!
Welcome! Welcome! <CUSTOM1021> <FullName> <CUSTOM1053> it is, isn't it? Are ya lookin' to enter the competition?
I'm sorry mate, we only allow each competitor to enter the competition three times, else you rich folks'd keep entering and that wouldn't be fair on the others!
Nice try <FullName>.  Ya should try again, see if ya can get a prize!
Well <Mister/Missus>, you're a fine shot ain't ya? Ya certainly deserve a prize ...
Here ya go then. We reward our best archers with something they'll find useful. Enjoy them, but don't waste 'em on a straw target, will ya!

Simply put, ya beat three opponents, and you'll be rewarded with some magic bolts or arrows. It costs just 10 golden lions to enter, but your last opponent will be a master, as he is chosen especially to stop us giving out too many prizes today. Interested, or ya want more detail?

Really? If ya don't know how to score in a competition, I can't see ya getting very far, but here goes ... Each round ya get six arrows. Ya score more than your opponent, then ya get through to the next round. Simple enough eh?

Ya keep ya score for the next round, so ya may be ahead or behind ya next opponent. Anyway, we use standard scoring: 1 point for white, 3 for black, 5 for blue, 7 for red, and of course a full 9 for gold. How does that sound? Are you in?
Well, Thunderstone rules is that the challenger wins in the event of a tie. Can't say fairer than that, can ya? Anyway, do I count you in?
Excellent! Let me just call over your opponent ...
A bit short of cash there are ya? Well I'm sure ya just left it somewhere right? Best if ya go find it. 10 golden lions is the entry fee.
Your kidding me aren't ya mate? Ya can't enter on horseback!
I don't see enough quarrels in your quiver there mate. 18 ya need, unless ya plan to go out of the competition before the end!
Not right now.
You're not wrong.
Thanks.
What are the rules of the competition?
I need to know how scoring is handled.
Well, what if there is a tie?
Yes, I am interested.
[End Conversation]
I am a bit busy right now. Is it important?
I hear you.
I'm sure you understand that I'm a bit busy right now, and you'll be keen to order the new grave, so I'll leave you to it, eh?
Well I offered to help out and the offer is still open. I'm not saying it was me that did it, but isn't the important thing to replace the grave, not trouble the Law?
Well, I must be going. Good luck finding the culprit.
I agree, and the Crown Office is the right place to report this.
Well, I am sure that I can cover the cost of a new grave as a gesture of goodwill, though of course I maintain it was nothing to do with me.
Then what do you want?
Alright then, I'll do so, if that is what is necessary. As a knight such behavior is not above me, so I am sure I can manage this to help your father know peace...
An excellent punishment. Perhaps you will learn something from it, <CUSTOM1022>.
Fifty is the best I can do...
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Oh very well then, if that is what it takes to end this...
Again?
Look, I can manage fifty, alright?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Oh very well then, if that is what it takes to end this...
Are we fine now?
Well, that's good. I'm just glad to help out, that's all. Here's ten golden lions to cover the cost.
I'm sure you understand that I'm a bit busy right now, and you'll be keen to order the new grave, so I'll leave you to it, eh?
B-b-but, I...I  never did!
Your family must be disgusted with the shame you are bringing on them.
That was disgraceful behavior. You should be ashamed.
That was disgraceful behavior. You should be ashamed.
Not now, please!
Why would I want to talk about graves?
Greetings.
Well...er, what's that got to do with me?
What? What's this rubbish? Whoever told you that is a liar!
Why would you believe someone else's word over mine?
Well...perhaps...there's no need to be hasty! I didn't do it, you understand, but as one aspiring knight to another, I am sure there is something I can do to help out?
Well, I am sure that I can cover the cost of a new grave as gesture of goodwill!
Well, that's good. I'm just glad to help out, that's all. Here's ten golden lions to cover the cost.
No, we're done.
Just remember I'm watching you.
I believe them.
Maybe they lied...It was probably someone else. I'll leave you in peace then.
Perhaps I'll report this to the Crown Office and let them handle it.
Like what?
Fair enough. I accept your offer.
This is a matter for the Crown Office to resolve. If you're guilty, you'll pay for it.
Perhaps. Tell me your offer.
No, I want the culprit punished.
Let's go.
I'm going to report this and see what happens.
You did it, and it's time to pay for it.
That's not good enough.
Go and say a penance every day over my father's grave.
<StartCheck>[Intimidate]</Start> I want a hundred golden lions, or I'll force it out of you!
<StartCheck>[Persuade]</Start> I want a hundred golden lions for the insult to my family.
That'll do.
I want to talk to you about my father's grave.
Good.
We are done.
Fair enough. I accept your offer.
You were seen defacing it.
No, nevermind.
Never mind.
Someone defaced my father's grave.
Because it was you.
Because you defaced my father's.
Oh, then I shall leave you in peace.
Anything else <CUSTOM1021> <FirstName>??
Yes <CUSTOM1021> <FirstName>?
Where shall I move to?
I'll do that now.
I'm done.
Move to your post.

The right flank

JOBS GO HERE

A client of mine has had a certain item stolen from them and wants it returned. It seems that this item is now in the hands of the priest Magnus, in the Shrine of Tempus. It is not certain how the item got into the priest's hands, but it needs to be returned. Doing so pays 800 golden lions. Does that interest you?
Excellent. When you have it, just bring it to me and you shall be paid. Try to make sure the horn is not damaged.
When the tournament runs you can get access to the grounds by just heading over to the east side of town.
Sir Hawklin's castle is at the south end of Thunderstone. You can't miss it, it's a big stone structure.
It's at the south end of town.
The Shrine of Tempus caters for all. Head to the main square and it's on the south side.
Well the Furniture's Fate is the nearest, on the east side of the square.
Here you are then...
Tell me.
What do you need?

Yes. You are fortunate. I have done a little research on this for the new smith in Wangle's Livery. I'll tell you what I told her. I have some ingredients, but they are stolen. Do you wish to take a look?
Here you are then...
I never give the name of my clients.
A murder? That doesn't come cheap, although it can be done without links to you.
I don't negotiate this...the cost is a thousand golden lions.
That's the cost of silence. Take it or leave it.
Did you want something else?
It is as good as done. <CUSTOM1022> will be heard from no more.
<FirstName>, no matter what pain this knight caused you, to murder them for it is plain wrong.
I cannot <FirstName>. If you go through with this then you are not a worthy companion, nor the instrument of Torm that I hoped.
Then you must continue without me. I do not know you <CUSTOM1021> <LastName>. You are not the <man/woman> I knew.
Shall we get back to business then?
I'm still gathering it. Have patience and I'll get you everything there is to be had.
Then you should make your requests through me. I am not telling you my client's name.
I've given you all the information I can. There's no more to be had.
Easy enough. How urgently do you need it? Quicker you want it, the more it'll cost, as I'll need to hire more people.
That'll cost you 10 golden lions. How does that sound?
That'll cost you 20 golden lions. How does that sound?
That'll cost you 50 golden lions. How does that sound?
Your choice. Was there anything else?
How long then?
Good. Come back later and I'll tell you what I know.
Hmmm...well first I need to set a couple of ground rules.
Then we are done. Did you want something else?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Well, I know that Lord Marvin Huntcrown does like to sell his trophies, so I suppose it does no harm you knowing the horn was his.

I am a go-between. I protect the identity of my clients, as I protect the identity of those that work for me. I will not tell you who requires a job done, but nor will I tell my clients who is doing the job. That way I carry all the risks, but I know also all the secrets.
Everyone needs something done. I am the one that can make it happen, and that makes me useful. It's only secrets that protect me though, from those that want me silenced after a job is done.
Understand that I deliver on a job I undertake. You must promise to do the same if you accept it.
Then let's get down to business...
Exactly.
<StartAction>[Alice Broadhand takes a long look at your companions]</Start>
Woman, why are you looking at me like that?
I am measuring you up of course. You'll do I think.
Are we acceptable then?
You I know...
Threats do not concern me. Your death would shortly follow mine.
I don't think we have had the pleasure of meeting.
Well you are polite...but are you appropriate I wonder? We shall have to see...
Madam, I know you have a reputation for...uneven scruples. Please keep your offers appropriate.
I did so last time. I shall do so again.
Edgar Truesilver, a gentleman and a fine servant of Thunderstone...I shall try to meet your request.
Alice. No games today.
Very well Lacinda. You at least I know I can trust.
Is there something wrong?
Not this time, Lady Kathryn....
Lady Kathryn Hawklin. You are welcome of course.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Well, I know that Lord Marvin Huntcrown does like to sell his trophies, so I suppose it does no harm you knowing the horn was his.

Unfortunately I don't believe I have any jobs at present, or at least, any that are appropriate for the present company. I have clients to respect, but also I try not to offer work to those that do not need it, do not appreciate it, or might otherwise complicate matters.
Never mind. Did you want something else?
Good <QuarterDay> to you.
It means there's work to be had, but not work I would approve of.
As I said, I think for the benefit of all. Was there something else?
I'm not sure which of those categories I fall under, but basically <FirstName>, she's saying she won't talk in front of me.
I may have some work for you soon, so come back later. At present there is nothing.
I do not have any jobs at present, but I shall keep you in mind.
Oh, that is wonderful! I always liked Sir Gilbert, so I will be delighted when we give our client a piece of information that is useless to them!

The deal stands of course. You get paid as agreed and I will have to deal with the anger of the client. Don't worry, we both did what was asked of us. It can't be helped if the answer is not what the client wanted to hear.
Just do not tell him the information came from me. He will assume you knew from another source. He is not exactly discreet about his trophies.
Here you go: 200 golden lions as agreed. You have my thanks for a job well done.
Oh, that is wonderful! I always liked Sir Gilbert, so I will be delighted when we give our client a piece of information that is useless to them!

The deal stands of course. You get paid as agreed and I will have to deal with the anger of the client. Don't worry, we both did what was asked of us. It can't be helped if the answer is not what the client wanted to hear.
Here you go: 200 golden lions as agreed. You have my thanks for a job well done.
And?
I find you unconvincing. Tell me now, is this the truth?
A shame. Many years of practiced lying on my part means that I am good at spotting a lie like the one you just told me.
Not only did you fail to find the entrance, but you tried to conceal the fact from me. I consider the job closed. Should we work together in the future, I would suggest a more direct approach.
Was there anything else?
There's a lesson there I think. Honesty is generally the best policy I find.

I need someone who will take a look around inside Hawklin Castle. My client wishes to know whether there is a secret entrance into that castle and apparently have found nothing from the outside. The job pays two hundred golden lions, since the information is valuable.
Well done <FirstName>! You just lost us 200 golden lions!
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Really? I am surprised that my other source could not find it...are you sure?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Well, you have been diligent and I appreciate that. My client will welcome this news. Thank you.
I always appreciate a straight answer. I believe you at least looked, and since that is the case, you will be paid as originally offered.
Here you are, 200 golden lions, and I shall consider the job completed.
Was there anything else?
But you earned it for doing the job. Successful or not, I always pay up.
I have the information you needed. Do you want to hear it now?

Polter's Fort is an old castle that was deserted when it was almost complete. The reasons for its desertion revolve around superstitions that the site of the fort was haunted. You should visit Magnus in the Shrine of Tempus for the full tale.

The inner wall and keep of the fort were largely completed, but the curtain wall and moat were not. The fort is still defensible, though some parts of the keep have collapsed and it has been deserted for centuries.
No, but clearly it will not be on the upper floor, so that should narrow your search.

The design of the keep was standard for the time. It contains three levels: the chapel and private quarters on the upper floor; the barracks, stores, armory and Great Hall on the lower floor, and some cells in the basement. The keep gate opens into a short passageway that runs into the Great Hall.
That is it, really. There were some rumors also that the keep might be inhabited, which I couldn't substantiate, but wouldn't surprise me in view of all these raids.
A pleasure doing business with you.
Any back ways into the keep?
No, the keep has only one door, but there is a postern gate in the surrounding wall.
That is everything there is that can be found on the fort. If there was anything else, I'd have found it.
This is very high quality information. Was there anything else?
Greetings <FirstName>. Any progress with collecting that item I asked for?
I see. I suppose that demonstrates you are resourceful, but not that you are trustworthy.
Well, I shall consider hard before I offer you any more work. Next time, it will be something where I know you can't cross me. I don't need to learn the lesson twice.
As you like then. Was there anything else?
So was there something you wanted?
I don't think that I can trust you <FirstName>. I think you had the horn, but that you chose to do something else with it.
Well, I shall consider hard before I offer you any more work. For the moment, I will give you the benefit of the doubt. Was there anything else you wanted?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Yes, that is what I had heard, but I thought I would check with you. I shall have to find another way to get the horn, or another horn...
Yes, that is what I had heard, but I thought I would check with you. I shall have to find another way to get the horn, or another horn...
No matter. I thought you could face down Magnus, but he is strong, like all priests of Tempus. I shall have to find another way.
Was there anything else?
No. You are no longer any use in this matter, as Magnus knows you want the horn. I'll find another. Was there anything else you wanted?
Excellent. Hand it over then and I shall pay you as agreed.
Excellent! Here is the gold that I promised you: 800 golden lions. It's a very good price, more than the horn is worth, but I'm not one to argue with generous clients.
Your choice. Are you certain? I will not offer the job again.
All my clients are confidential. I told you that.
It looks like I can depend on you, <FirstName>. Perhaps I can help you in some way?
Threats do not concern me. Your death would shortly follow mine. Are you going to give me the horn or not? I am paying more than it's worth for it.
Don't think too long, my client won't wait forever. Was there anything else?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Well, I know that Lord Marvin Huntcrown does like to sell his trophies, so I suppose it does no harm you knowing the horn was his.
Just don't tell him the information came from me. He will assume you knew from another source. It's not likely he'll care anyway; Lord Huntcrown is not exactly discreet about his trophies.
Well I have already told you it was Huntcrown. You have a poor memory. Are you going to give me the horn or not? I am paying more than it's worth for it.
Well hello. If you're looking for Alice, then that means you're either looking to get a job done, looking for a job yourself, or looking to get rid of something. Which is it?
Aye, I'll take unwanted items off your hands, for a price, and not ask any question where you got them from. Let me see what you have...

Then you should sell them elsewhere. I buy what others don't want, but I don't need a reputation for ripping you off for honest goods. Ask Colebriar there if you want to sell regular goods. Otherwise...
<FirstName>, I'll go with whatever you decide. I am happy to be judged by your decisions.
A job's a job, and the pay is good. Why not do it?
This task doesn't sound like a good idea. If we want Hawklin's help, this can't help.
Well?
I'm not sure it matters. Is that the kind of job we want to take if we intend to be on Sir Gilbert Hawklin's good side?
We should avoid this task I think.
He doesn't need to know.
He doesn't need to know.
Good. Whatever you discover, report back to me. I have a few eyes of my own in the castle, so I'll know if you made a serious try...but I'm sure you're not the type to cross me.
Was there anything else you wanted?
Was there anything else?
No, but clearly it will not be on the upper floor, so that should narrow your search. Anything else?
Hello again, <CUSTOM1021> <FirstName> <CUSTOM1053>.
What do you need?
Some help I charge for, some I don't. Let's hear it.
Well, I suppose I can offer you a rumor for free, or maybe just a piece of gossip. Let's see...
BROKEN DIALOGUE
A tip for you, since you look like one to take opportunities.
Ever heard the rumor about the White Stag? The hunters have a local legend about this creature that is too fast to catch. Several lords have declared it their aim to hunt this animal.

There was a murder last week. Some unfortunate knight new in to Thunderstone who was lured into the forest and slain. Thiodor Hurim, the Crown's agent, thinks that he was lured out by a woman claiming she had been attacked, and was then set upon.
No more details unless you take the job, that's the rule on this one.
My source told me that she saw the merchant Imelda leaving Thunderstone alone one evening. In times like these, who'd want to do a thing like that?

Last time Valetto's ship was in Thunderstone, it looked like it had ivory on board. He's supposed to be a lumber merchant. Maybe he's secretly carrying a load for the merchant Imelda? Odd really. Those two always pretend to hate each other.

There's a lot of movement along the Sembian border at the moment. Could be they're preparing for an invasion. That would explain why the Purple Dragons spend more time in their barracks than chasing raiders.
Ever heard the rumor about the White Stag? The hunters have a local legend about this creature that is too fast to catch. Several lords have declared it their aim to hunt this animal.
They say the new smith is excellent and she used to forge magic weapons. Of course nowadays with such a shortage of regular arms she rarely gets the chance.
I am sure she would welcome the opportunity to work on magic again.
It is true that she is a very good smith.
Ever heard the rumor about the White Stag? The hunters have a local legend about this creature that is too fast to catch. Several lords have declared it their aim to hunt this animal.
They're all looking for it in Hullack Forest. They'd be better off looking along the banks of the Lake from what I've heard.
Well there's a lot of fear in Thunderstone at the moment. Something is stalking the streets at night.
Excellent. Then let me give you the rest of the details. The item that needs to be returned is a unicorn's horn...
It's certainly something to fear, but it doesn't come from outside the town, or so I've heard...but then, perhaps it's just gossip.
Oh really! How silly!
Is it now, Lady Kathryn? I wonder...
A tip for you, since you look like one to take opportunities.
Look out for Bodak's Teeth in any of the markets. If you find one, take it over to the smith in Wangle's Livery. She's a master crafter and can make magic with such a thing.

This is a very old rumor that has persisted for a long time, but they say there is a castle out on Lake Wyvernwater that rises and falls beneath the waves, and that it can only be found when there is mist on the lake. I don't give it much credence, but you asked for rumors.
I can't help wondering how Valetto is the only merchant whose ships have not once been pirated. Something to think about there I am sure.
I can't really understand how, with all this piracy on Lake Wyvernwater, no one has once caught any of the pirates.
Pirates seem to wear a lot of guises these days.
I hope you are not insinuating that the navy are not trying? My cousin Ayesunder is the admiral.
Magnus for certain will not part with it, for he must know it's properties are particularly useful for making magic weapons, and as a priest of Tempus he will be too interested to let it go.
No, Edgar, I think it would be wiser to look nearer to home than the Cormyrian navy.
Only that some pirates are not always pirates. But then some pirates don't like a talker either, so I'll leave it at that.
Well the latest gossip is all about Sir Gilbert Hawklin. They say he is bankrupt and may have to sell his castle in Thunderstone.
I guess it was all the donations he made to get the new walls for Thunderstone built. A shame if it bankrupts him.
Well you shouldn't listen to such rubbish. My father's finances are fine, so please stop that gossip!
I peddle in gossip, young Kathryn, and a lot else besides that's undesirable. Even so I would be saddened to see Sir Gilbert go.
We're all discussing the jousting of course...
Sir Gilbert's nephew Sir Blakeney Hawklin is entering the next joust. He's quite fancied as he has a steady arm and a good strike on the center of the shield.
A knight who leans to the right would probably break his lance, conceding the point. Sir Gilbert's popular and any Hawklin does well with the crowd, so they'll enjoy his victories.
<StartAction>[You may add this to your journal in the completed section if you wish.]</Start>

No, the only thing that Magnus respects is force, but I for one don't want to see Magnus dead over this. Threaten him or intimidate him into releasing the horn. He respects strength. Convince him by the force of your will, and I am certain he will surrender the horn. I believe he might even admire you if you manage it, for he has a strong personality himself.
Anything more you want?
Inuman Insar the gnome will be riding in his first joust. He's quite fancied as he has a steady arm and a good strike on the center of the shield.
A knight who leans to the right would probably break his lance, and lose the point. Inuman's popular and if he does well will please the crowd.
<CUSTOM1065> is meant to be riding in the next joust. She's almost an unknown as she rarely enters the lists. A friend of mine works on her staff and she says <CUSTOM1065> is formidable.
I've heard that her favored strike is high and wide. Her opponents don't think she has the strength so they always duck behind their lances for extra force and end up being unhorsed.
Would be nice to see a lady win the next tournament I think. Would teach a few of the other jousters not to underestimate their opponents.
I agree. If only it could be me...but, I've chosen another route for now.
That's good information if she rides here, for I saw her do the same thing in a tourney in Arabel before the war.
Most of the current talk is about <CUSTOM1064>, the famous adventurer, who may ride in the next joust.

He is a famous jouster. The crowd will be very excited to watch him, but he has a serious weakness. He always strikes at the helm. A client of mine once paid for a way to beat him. The simplest answer was just to keep his head down in the joust, nothing more sinister than that.
As I said, he respects force. He may even threaten you back, but he won't strike you over this.
I'd very much like to see <CUSTOM1064> ride. He has a reputation as a doughty fighter on foot too.
The main talk is about the next tournament. I reckon <CUSTOM1063> has a good chance, don't you? His main weakness is that he always aims low to the left.
If one of his opponents notices, they'll just lean right to avoid him. Otherwise, though he has a good chance.
It's true. I saw him ride in Marsember once and he did  the same thing there.
<CUSTOM1062> is quite fancied in the jousting in the next tournament but he always aims low. I believe one of the other knights will beat him easily as long as they don't lower their shield.
I've watched a lot of jousts, and you can easily concede a point that way; they get a clean strike and break their lance.
Everyone is talking about young <CUSTOM1061> and that he'll win the next joust, but you watch him closely if you ever think of riding against him. He always goes for the helm.
Good looking boy though, Sir Azar. I'd like to see him do well.
<StartAction>[You may add this to your journal in the completed section if you wish.]</Start>
Anything more you want?

Whether you succeed in intimidating him or not, Magnus will not hold it against you. Force he respects. If he wins he will take it as a test from Tempus. If you win, he will take it as a victory for Might, and again the will of Tempus.
Cousin Azar? By Torm, that's absolutely right, he does too!
His opponent almost always raises their shield in reflex and...bang! They're on the ground!
I know little of Polter's Fort, except it's name. If you are prepared to pay though I can have information gathered for you.
For five golden lions, I can tell you who might know.
Threats bore me. Let's try a more reasonable approach.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> I think you actually might too. You wouldn't get very far, but it's not worth us all dying for five golden lions.
Then I can't tell you anything.

This place could do with the touch of the Morninglord! A little cheer, some light...perhaps we should seek a bard for our adventures!
I am glad to be out of Thunderstone though, even so. I get stifled in our castle!

Well, you are the leader, so the decision is yours. I hate to leave a job undone though, so any time you are in Thunderstone, come into the Sign of Thunder and see if I'm there. I will be more than willing to come with you.
Father never lets me out.
In many ways it reminds me of my ancestral home in Suzail. That was a cold and loveless place...all hard stone and leaks in the roof. We never had enough money to fix it.
Now of course, I don't have such worries. King Azoun took that house along with any money we had left.
I am sure that it will all work out for the best though Lacinda. With your help now, it will soon be recognised you're no traitor.
You have a lot to learn about human nature, Godfroy. I expect what we do here to make no difference to anyone's opinion except mine, and that's the one that counts.
Well I am certain that people will soon realize they misjudged you.
And rightly so! The Cormearils have been treacherous once too often!

The King did you an injustice I would say. Law and order are important, especially in times like these, but you are only distantly related to the traitors in the Abraxus Affair. It must hurt to have been branded with their treachery.
Ha! Maybe the King did us a favor taking that house! I hated it, but the label that goes with it...that I never earned.
Well they say that some traits are hereditary. Let's just hope that treachery isn't one of them.
None that are more important than this, so think about it.
Well child, wisdom clearly hasn't passed from your father to you, so perhaps I haven't inherited treachery!
Well, kings are not infallible it's true, though King Azoun IV was amongst the best.
It's hard to imagine it was built by Cormyrians when you see it now filled with such evil.
King Galaghard must have built this place to keep evil at bay. All he achieved was to make them a new stronghold.
It is very sad to see good deeds end this way.
Was Galaghard evil then?
I don't think he did it deliberately.
Well of course not! I know little of Galaghard, but we have him to be thankful for defeating the Witch Lords.
Him and the elves.
General dialogue in underground caves, WC. XXX
Then TO BATTLE!
Something lives in here, and it smells very bad.
Nothing good could smell that bad. I think we should be ready for danger.
I have a tendency to agree with you on this one Godfroy. The memory it stirs is not a good one, though I can't think why.
Well let's take a look around, then get out quick before I faint.
Fine, but keep your weapons handy.
This smell is familiar. Where have I smelt it?
I can't place it, but it smells like mold.
Or something like it...
That rules out pirates or smugglers, but what could it be?
I can smell salt on the breeze. We must be approaching the lake.
I'll have a go if you like...
Text: 에. 아마도. 자노스가 네 물건 좀 뒤져볼게. 감정할 수 있는 게 발견되면 말해주지. 충분하지?

TextEng: The water is brackish in the lake, almost like seawater. That's why farms are not common on the lake shore.
I even read there are sharks in the lake!
I have read the same thing, something about a gate to the elemental plane of water... but unless we are intending to swim, I think we are likely safe from them on this quest.

When we decided we had to move from the King's Forest, my mother thought we should become fishermen on the lake. Father and I thought it would be better to go with your family, <FirstName>, and continue farming.
It's what we knew best after all, so it didn't seem such a bad decision. Sometimes, I can't help regretting it.

Don't regret it, Godfroy. You had no idea what would happen. I for one am proud of the efforts you are making now to stop such things happening again. I am certain that Torm is guiding your hand in this.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
No, it is not revenge I want, but to stop such a dreadful thing happening to others.
I once sailed on the lake with my cousin Ayesunder. It is not really such a big stretch of water, and it was always an embarassment to him that he could never find the pirates there.
Fine, what do you need?
I read somewhere there are sharks in the lake. I'm not sure I'd want to sail on it.
Where magic is concerned, you can never be sure of anything. Your cousin must have endured a lot of comments. Well I know how that can feel...
For a Cormaeril, it must be far harder, though yes, he has suffered a lot of criticism. People are always too quick to search for traitors these days, and blame treachery for a lack of results.

Well I know that! But I suppose it is only to be expected. My extended family opposed the Royal Family once too often. I must pay for that. I only hope you do not become a victim of such mutterings, Edgar Truesilver.
And I hope you do not suffer much longer for the failings of your family, Lacinda.
I hope that too...
What an odd place.
Torm preserve us, but that is a very nasty smell!
I think it's coming from those toadstools there.
And...oh...by Tyr...what a stench!
Who is in need of this aid?
And...oh...Lord of Battles, what is that awful smell?
And...oh...Sweet Lathander...what a stench!
Careful on the bridge, it's slippery.
This bridge looks fairly recent. Some of the castle must have got filled with debris over the years and Wyvernvapor's trying to dig it out.
Oh! I really hate bats!
Don't worry, Lady Kathryn, bats are harmless and the least of our worries.
Er, thanks...I think, Edgar, though that didn't really make me feel much better!
I shall guard you Lady Kathryn, have no fear of that.
I can look after myself, thank you very much!
No offence intended Lady Kathryn. You have already shown us your skills.

The skills I have always given my King and country are the same ones I offer you: my skill with the blade and my knowledge of battle. I am regarded as a fine warrior, but also due to long years of dedication to the service of Torm, I am a recognised paladin, able to meet evil with the divine powers of The Loyal Fury, Torm himself.
Very well.
Oh I'm sorry, Edgar! I didn't mean to sound unkind, you just sounded so stuffy!
I take my duties seriously...too seriously perhaps, but I know your father would never forgive me if I returned and you did not.
Somehow that doesn't surprise me.
Bats are harmless, Kathryn. You shouldn't believe all that superstition about them.
Anyway, don't fear, <FirstName> and I are with you.
I appreciate that Godfory.
This is a strange place to leave a pair of mirrors.
These are clearly magic mirrors of some sort. I have heard of mirrors that don't reflect light, but reflect instead only magic.
Well the mirrors are large; small enough to carry, but not for any extended time. I am guessing these mirrors are used for something here in the castle.
The Keeper mentioned something about mirrors and beams involved in a puzzle. We should probably take these.
Who do you want me to lay hands on?
They're not much use. I can't even fix my hair with these!
I think they must be important, otherwise they would not just be left standing here.
Well they look useless to me, but if you want to take them <FirstName>, go ahead.
These are not ordinary mirrors. Look, their surface is shiny but they don't reflect anything.
Let's take them. They must have a use.
Perhaps they are some leftover from older times?
I guess that must be the Mythallar.
We do not have the knowledge or the tools necessary to break a Mythallar. We must find out how it powers the castle, and break whatever channels its power.
This is not something that my sword or my faith can conquer. I hope you understand these things better than I, <FirstName>.
I suppose the answers must lie here somewhere within the castle.
Very well.
The question is, how do we shut off the Mythallar's power? Clearly we can't just climb up and stop it. There must be another way.
It's very pretty isn't it? Seems a shame to try and stop it working.
Oh child! Why can't you concentrate on the task in hand? It is for your father's good that we deal with this thing. Let us concentrate.
Well I expect there's some reason you came too, Lacinda. No doubt some dark, secret reason that only a Cormaeril would understand.

Child, I came for <FirstName>, and <he/she> knows it. I'm sure it makes you feel good to throw the past treacheries of my family at my feet, but your family is no more noble than mine, even if it enjoys higher favor.
I just said it was pretty, that's all.
You are right. I will concentrate on the task in hand.
Look at the state of this place! The water must come in here all the time!
I thought this place would be more...well magical, and less horrible. Why would a dragon want to live here?
I don't think I will even attempt to guess, Lady Kathryn. Dragons are not something I know that much about.
What is it you wish me to cast?
It does seem a pretty nasty place to live, doesn't it?
Because dragons live in the real world, child, not in fairy tales, and generally they are not the gentle, playful creatures you've read about in all of your books!
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
Although that wouldn't apply to Wyvernvapor; Mist Dragons are at home in water.
Or so they say.
Although that wouldn't apply to Wyvernvapor; Mist Dragons are at home in water according to the scripts I have read about them.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
This chamber stinks and it's big enough to house the dragon, so I think it must be Wyvernvapor's lair. It looks like we're in luck though. The dragon is away. We should use our time wisely.
Maybe we can shut down the Mythallar and make our escape before the dragon returns.
Upon whom should I cast it?
This castle is very odd. It may seem deserted, but I thought I saw something move up on the roof.
If you look up at the top of the keep, you can see a watermark. I think the top of the castle never gets totally submerged. It's possible something might live up there.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack. Maybe we should look for somewhere safer to tie a horse than that hitching post.
I'm not sure. It's very difficult to see in this mist.
Look over there, on the other side of the chasm! There's a cave with some steps.
Though I don't see a way across this chasm.
We could possibly jump a horse across. There's room for a run-up.
I think we should stick to our mission though. After all the castle won't be in there.
At least, that's my view.
Very well.
I agree. We have a task that we should stick to.
The Mythallar might be though, or a secret way in.
Well, I suppose that is possible.
Maybe we could use a rope to get across? I have one in my pack.
It's not a bad idea if we want to get across.
If we want to get across, that might be a way.
But would that be safe?
Perhaps it's a smuggler's den?
For once child, you might be right.
Well we've found the castle...
Now we must find the Mythallar. Now that I am certain we are on the right track, my heart relishes the battle. Torm is with us, I am certain.
I'm sure that the end of our troubles is not far away.
Now to find the dragon. Can you believe it? We're actually looking for a dragon! It's like those tales about dragons in the history books...
"Then Kathryn and <FirstName> approached the great castle..."
It is a nice picture Kathryn. I'll look forward to hearing the full version when you are done with it.
Your father enjoys his tales, though I haven't heard him tell one since the war.
No, a lot left our lives when my brothers were killed and Father lost his arm. It's rare for him to even smile these days.
Some of the troubles of the realm rest on his shoulders. Let us continue on now and see what we can do to lift them. Remember though, it is the Mythallar we seek, not the dragon.

Child, your imagination is running away again. Try to remember that dragons are dangerous and spiteful lizards, not tales from your childhood. In any event we are looking for the Mythallar, not the dragon.
Well actually I have head that Wyvernvapor is not a dangerous dragon.
Very well.
Well I'm sure we'll find out soon enough.

I have heard many people moan about the prices in the Six Coffers Trading Coster, but they say you can't beat it for variety. I couldn't tell you if it's true though. Most of my equipment came either from my family or the army.
Well <FirstName>, as far as I am concerned, I still owe you one for rescuing me from the barrows. If you'll have me, I am ready to fight at your side once more.
Text: 자노스에게 다시 합류하자고 요청하러 온 거지?

TextEng: Fine, if that is what you wish I shall remain here in the hope that you change your mind.
Text: 젠장! 그럼 네가 정신 차릴 때까지 여기 있겠어.

TextEng: <StartHighlight>Edgar is currently unconscious and will likely die if he is not given aid very soon.</Start>
Text: <StartHighlight>자노스는 현재 의식이 없고, 도움을 받지 못하면 곧 죽을 것입니다.</Start>

TextEng: Was that death? A strange experience...Torm grant me I shan't face that again!
Text: 흥. 네가 제대로 했다면 자노스가 이런 불쾌함을 겪지 않아도 됐을 텐데.

TextEng: By Torm, Of course I will!
There's work to be done, <FirstName>. When you're ready, then so am I.
Text: 여기 남아 있겠어. 가고 싶으면 가.

TextEng: Good <QuarterDay> <FullName>.
You are not worthy to be called a Cormyrian. I will not help you.
Very well, I am a willing student...
Text: 자노스는 원하는 대로 실력과 능력을 키울 거다.

TextEng: What is it?
Sounds like you have. I caught a couple more skulking about too, but probably the victory would not have been possible without your help.
Didn't you have companions with you?

That...that is very bad news. These barrows are ancient places. Evil, some might say, though that is not so. There's much in them we don't understand. I can only hope your brother recovers from his madness. Most of the other ill effects in these places are temporary.

I did not see him, but I have not just been standing here. I took my remaining troops on a sweep. One of the scouts said they saw a man running from the barrows. I had assumed it was a deserter, but maybe it was your brother.
I take it they did not survive?
I see. Battle is like that sometimes...takes friends earlier than we wish it.
I've lost a lot of soldiers, but it could have been worse. I thank you sincerely, <FullName>. It is probable you have saved several lives. We must get back and report to Sir Hawklin.
No, can't you hear? There's still fighting going on somewhere. See if you can find it and help out.
I'll meet you back here once the job is done.
Fine <FirstName>, if you think that is a good idea.
I am not certain, but it's pretty systematic. Either they know they're good for loot, or whoever's behind these raids is looking for something, though I have no idea what.
We tracked a large force of raiders into this barrow, and had them trapped. Things were going well, when one of the scouts posted outside warned me a second force was approaching.

They never strike a barrow with two forces, so either they were tipped off by a scout, or they got lost and hit the wrong barrow. Whichever, the second force got here before we could disengage, and it was our turn to get trapped.

Me and a small group of men got forced into a side passage. We managed to kill our foes and drive our way back to the main branch. The rest of my men got driven deeper into the barrow. That's where the fighting is, and that's where I want you to go and help out.
No, you save yours, I've got my own. I'll be ready for combat again in a few minutes, but don't waste time waiting for me. Go and help the rest of the men!
Then why are you here?
Are you serious? I suppose you were just walking in the forest right?
Only Sir Hawklin knows I'm here, so he must have sent you to help. Stop wasting time now. Men are dying while we talk.
Excellent. I'll be back on my feet soon enough, then I'll do my own bit of hunting.
I don't know who you are...but I hope you came to help! I'm Edgar Truesilver.
For countering the evils we are bound to find on this quest, I can think of no better set of skills. Will you take me?
What do you need?
Well, <LastName>, my injuries have put me out of the battle for the moment. Are you up to hunting hobgoblins?
Well, that means you'll have to help if you're expecting me to come with you.
There's more hobgoblins and a few ogres deeper in the barrows. Can you clean out the rest while I gather the rest of my troops?
Excellent. I'll be back on my feet soon enough, then I'll do my own bit of hunting.
I'll meet you back here once the job is done.
I have no idea what natural protections are found here, but you're certain to find hobgoblins and maybe ogres amongst the raiders.
I am not certain, but it's pretty systematic. Either they know they're good for loot, or whoever's behind these raids is looking for something, though I have no idea what.
We tracked a large force of raiders into this barrow and had them trapped. Things were going well, when one of the scouts posted outside warned me a second force was approaching.

They never strike a barrow with two forces, so either they were tipped off by a scout, or they got lost and hit the wrong barrow. Whichever, the second force got here before we could disengage and it was our turn to get trapped.

I got forced into a side passage, a small group of soldiers with me. We managed to kill our foes and drive our way back to the main branch. The rest of my troops got driven deeper into the barrow. That's where the fighting is and that's where I want you to go and help out.
Very sensible, I would say. Is there anything else?
No, you save yours, I've got my own. I'll be ready for combat again in a few minutes, but don't waste time waiting for me. Go and help the rest of the troops!
Then why are you here?
Are you serious? I suppose you were just walking in the forest right?
Only Sir Hawklin knows I'm here, so he must have sent you to help. Stop wasting time now. Men are dying while we talk.
If they're beyond you, they're likely beyond me too. I'll more likely have to smash my way past any locks, but I'll do my best. Was there anything else?
That's a relief. Sneaking about sits very ill with me. Is there anything else?
There's a big difference between trying and succeeding. I'll do my best, but I make more noise than a charging boar. Was there anything else?
I'm not sure you'll find me much use in that, but I'll try. Is there anything else?
Agreed, I'll keep an eye out for enemies. It's a good plan <CUSTOM1020>. Anything more?
I am sorry if I have failed in that respect. How can I help you better on this?
That seems a little wasteful of our resources <FirstName>, but I am sure you know what you are doing. Is there anything else you need?
The direct approach. It lacks subtlety, but I prefer it that way. Is there anything else?
My name is Edgar Truesilver, son of Sir Edrick Truesilver, from a fairly minor branch of the Truesilver family. I serve Cormyr in whatever way that I can.
Very well, then. Is there anything else?
Just tell me where you want me.
Just don't kill everything before I can get into combat! Is there anything else?
Of course. Is there anything else?
For the tough work, it's the best way. Is there anything else?
Well, if you insist <FirstName>, but I am not the land's best shot, that's for certain. Is there anything else?
I'm glad we're in agreement on that, I'm useless with a bow. Is there anything else?
I'm sorry <FirstName>, but my training is not up for discussion. All of my energies are focussed in becoming a weapon of Torm. A true paladin cannot stray from that path.
But if there is anything else on tactics, we can discuss that. Was there?
Yes?

I am an officer in the Purple Dragons, but also I am on friendly terms with Sir Gilbert Hawklin. My commission in the army is not a regular one: I have earned from the Royal Family in person, the right to come and go as I please. It can cause trouble with Oversword Laheralson, the commander in Thunderstone, as you have already seen, but the benefit is always for Cormyr.
You don't need to worry about me, <FirstName>, I have fought in more battles than I can remember. A few scratches goes with the territory.
Text: "다 완전 끝내줘. 더할 나위 없지. 뭐... 내가 엄청 부자에 글래머한 하플링 아가씨들 하렘에 둘러싸여 있으면 더 좋겠지만... 그건 당장은 안 되겠지, 하하하!"

TextEng: Was there anything else?
Yes. In fact I feel Torm's hand in all of this. Meeting you was no coincidence, I am sure of it.
These are just scratches <FirstName>, nothing to worry about. I've had worse shaving.
Text: "프흣, 난 걱정 마. 그냥 긁힌 상처 몇 개야."

TextEng: Was there anything else?
I've been worse. All this blood can be really tough to get out of the armor though. If you could spare me some bandages, I wouldn't say no.
Text: "아까 좀 엉망이 되긴 했지, 헤. 볼 것까지는 없어."

TextEng: Else I'm sure I'll manage.
These wounds will leave me with a few more scars, that's for certain. I am in a worse state than in any battle I can remember. I mustn't grumble though, wounds are to be expected.
Text: "그냥... 몇 군데 긁혔을 뿐이야, 별거 아냐." 그는 얼굴을 찡그리며 빈 팔로 배에서 솟는 심한 피를 틀어막으려 합니다.

TextEng: Well I can't actually see anything <FirstName>. I was hoping you might actually have noticed by now! Anyway, I'm not sure if there is anything you can do about it, but...
Text: "괜찮을 거야, 아마. 근데 여기가 정말 어두운 건지... 내가 진짜 눈이 먼 건지 말해 줄래? 살짝 걱정돼서."

TextEng: I'm fine, nothing I can't handle, just feel like I've caught fire, that's all. I think something might have poisoned me a little bit.
Text: "어이! 완전 멀쩡해-내 혈관을 타고 흐르는 불덩이만 빼면 말이지. 그건... 알아서 해결되겠지..."

TextEng: Now is such a time. I would like to join you on your current quest. I owe you one, <CUSTOM1020>, but this is also for Cormyr. Will you have me at your side?
No, I am fairly certain I've caught something. Disease always follows a soldier, I should know that, but this is a very bad time to be ill.
Text: "피부에 이상한 반점이 좀 생긴 것만 빼면 나쁘지 않아. 이거... 안 좋은 건가?"

TextEng: If you have something to cure me, I would appreciate your using it. Otherwise, I am certain I can manage.
I don't have anything else to say just now. Perhaps later.

I told you how the queen had laid out the truth about Elaine before me? That was a defining moment for me. She is a smart woman, Filfaeril. She put me in a place where my love and my duty were directly in opposition. One of them had to break. I chose to believe her, as I think she always knew I would. Duty won out over love.
I did not realize that I had never really made the choice in my heart. That came much later.

For the next weeks I was fighting almost continuously against the goblin hordes; at Arabel and in the King's Forest. Promotion came easily for the bravest and best and I was like one possessed. But death came equally easily.

Every time the dragon came, or one of the ghazneths, many of our best leaders and strongest War Wizards would be killed. In one such battle I came across a man lying trapped under his horse. It was the King.

I had him at my mercy. It was then that I realized that in my heart, Elaine was still there. My hand unconsciously was on my sword hilt. The King just looked me in the eye and said: "I always knew I could trust your loyalty, Edgar."
He never doubted me for a moment. It was like an absolution. I helped the King to his feet, and we were swept back into the battle in a moment...
I hope that you wouldn't have, <FirstName>. I believe you are stronger than that.
That is a story for another time, perhaps while we are on the march together, if you will have me?
That's a bad joke, <FirstName>.

Before we were sucked back into the fighting, the King turned to me and said: "Edgar Truesilver, I was trapped and you gave me my freedom today. I grant you the same, to come and go as you see fit, guided only by your own sense of duty, not that which has been laid upon you by Cormyr. I know you will choose wisely."

Aaah! It is along time since I have told anyone the whole of that story! Few know the test that I went through to earn the right to do as I see fit. I am glad I have told you too, <CUSTOM1020>. I think the King would have granted you the same rights.
Anyway, I have talked enough I would say.
After Elaine was banished, I felt lost for a long time. I must admit that my duty to King Azoun, and my hatred for him, were kept in balance. Only my devotion to Torm kept me strong.
I carried on as before.
I think the King knew I hated him, and perhaps he did not trust me either, but he continued to give me the privileges and duties I had performed before, as if nothing had happened.
I think I hated him most for that. He knew that my duty stopped me from taking action. That was a heavy bond of trust he placed on me, and I hated it.

War came. The ghazneths got loose, and Princess Alusair seemed lost. King Azoun summoned me to him one day, but when I arrived at the Audience Chamber, it wasn't the King who was there, but Queen Filfaeril.

The queen beckoned me forward, and said to me: "Edgar, I too share the belief that I have lost someone I love, so I understand the suffering that you have been feeling for so long. I have asked you here, to ease that pain..."
No problem. I shall wait here awhile yet, but I can't wait for ever.

"The King and Vangerdahast believe this is something you should never hear, that it will hurt you worse than you are hurting already, but as a woman, I think I understand matters of the heart better."

"I must tell you that even when Elaine Cormaeril was banished, there was a very strong suspicion of her loyalty to the crown that had nothing to do with the Abraxus Affair, but more to do with seeking another way through to the King. You."

"We have since discovered that Elaine is a member of the Fire Knives, the group of Cormyrian exiles that seek the assassination of the King and prominent nobles of the realm. The King thinks that to tell you this will hurt you too much for you to maintain your balance. Vangerdahast just thinks you won't believe it. Me? I think it will make you stronger if you know the truth."
That was a black day, <CUSTOM1020>, let's not talk about it anymore right now. Perhaps later I can finish my story.

I told you a little about the times of peace, didn't I? For me mostly times of boredom to be honest, <CUSTOM1020>. I guess you must have experienced something similar, else you would not have left Cormyr.
Good ones, I am certain, <CUSTOM1020>. Others thought I steadfastly did my duty, but...
Well, I did think about leaving Cormyr myself, often actually, but always my duty to the King and my training as a paladin kept me here.
I hungered for something exciting to happen in my life though, and I think I was probably not the best student in those times. Then one day my life changed completely.
I talk of a woman of course <FirstName>. No doubt you have guessed as much. Her name was Elaine, and she brought a sweetness to life that I would not have believed possible.
It hurts to think about it, to be honest. It's far too long since I thought of Elaine...
Excellent! <CUSTOM1020>, you shall not regret it!

One summer of love we had. It was very strange <CUSTOM1020>, a special kind of friendship I suppose it was more like, for we never discussed 'love'. We just knew it was there, unspoken, and we searched out each other's company whenever we could, both understanding our desire just to share time.
Who knows what would have become of us? We thought we had all the time in the world I guess, and never acted upon our love. We both had duties to perform and put them first.
That is was, <CUSTOM1020>. I am glad you understand it. But there was a complication.
I didn't say it, did I? Elaine was a Cormaeril, and when the plot to kill King Azoun came to light, the Cormaerils were found to be behind it. The Abraxus Affair it was called.
Elaine was not implicated as far as I knew, but she was from an important branch of the Cormaerils. She was banished with the rest of them.
That is what I believed too.

There is a route there you can take from the mainland, and as luck would have it you're very close to it. Work your way north along the cliff edge and you'll eventually come to a pathway leading down into the bay. Now it might look like there's no way to go from there, but there is <lad/lass>.
