Follow the sand bars west into the lake, and when the mist's on the water, they'll lead you right to an island, an island you'll never see when the mist is gone!

Not I. It's dangerous. I'd not want to make an enemy of the pirates or the dragon, and besides, there's wyverns that watch the sandbars. Likely they'd have a go at any Jack Tar trying to make the crossing alone.
For you maybe, my <lad/lass>, but that's not what I'm about. Go somewhere else if you're here to mock. This is my home.
I'm not so much in the mood for telling tales now.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> True enough. True enough.

This place is full of them <CUSTOM1052>. You know I once went up to Thunderstone to report it? Could have lost my head for that, but no one in town cared a jot, so mostly I sell my fish to the pirates nowadays. Stupid landlubbers. Maybe I should've been a pirate, not a fisherman.
Why, in the magic castle of course.
Hello there! I be Garth. What's your name then <lad/lass>?
Suit yourself. That's probably for the best anyway, as I'll just be calling you <lad/lass> or <CUSTOM1052> anyway!
Well that's a nice name, isn't it? I'm going to call you <lad/lass> or <CUSTOM1052> though. I can't remember names for more'n a few seconds anyway!
A shame. Some tales are better with a bit of liquor to wash them down.

Now, I ain't seen nout but pirates in these parts for a long time. I guess you've heard my reputation as a fine tale teller? You'll be wantin' to swap yarns about the high seas an' such no doubt, eh <lad/lass>?
What do you want to know about?
Well I'm here for another yarn, when you're a'passing.
I'm not so interested in that one right now.

Aye, the White Stag. A most wonderful looking beast it is. It comes up sometimes right to the edge of the chasm behind my house. I tried to follow it. Crossing the chasm with a rope was perilous. It's too big for a man to jump unaided, though a horse might.
When I got to the other side though, I had no hope of catching up to the stag on foot, and it soon disappeared into the trees.
Nothing thanks.
Tell me again about the White Stag.
You mentioned a mystical beast. Tell me more.
Then I'll be going.
That's a fine tale. Goodbye for now.
I have some Hultail Spirits.
I have some spirits.
I have some ale.
I have some wine.
Tell me again how to find the castle.
I've heard you have a tale to tell about a magic castle.
Whatever you tell me I'll take very seriously.
It's in my nature to believe what I hear until I see otherwise.
I'm hunting pirates and I think this is the place to find them.
Maybe you're right, but are you going to tell me this tale or not?
Is that a threat?
Let me ask you a question.
What tales do you have to tell?
No, I've had enough.
Yes
I'm on a quest to find this castle.
I like a good yarn as much as the next <man/woman>.
Where do the pirates go when the castle sinks?
Tell me how to find this castle.
Have you ever been to the castle?
That's very helpful. I'll be going now.
To have a laugh of course. Isn't that what silly tales are for?
Fine, I'll leave you to your silly tales.
<StartCheck>[Persuade]</Start> A good yarn's always worth a laugh. Tell it anyway.
Sorry. The truth is it's very important for me to hear about this castle.
What do you know about pirates?
Where do the pirates live?
Tell me more about this castle. You must have a good tale to tell.
I don't give my name to strangers.
My name is <FullName>.
I have nothing.
I have heard enough for now.
Thanks
Goodbye fools!
Death to the Cormyrian!
Szass Morg! The Witch Lord!
For the Witch Lord!
[This gate is locked. You will have to speak to the melee master if you wish to enter the general melee.]
What is it?
Will you let me go free then?
It's true. I am a slave.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Do you think a slave would know he has a secret treasury that can be entered from this very room?
The Witch Lord tells me nothing that is a secret.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> It's true that he has a secret treasury in this very room.
I hear him open it sometimes, but being blind has stopped me ever finding it.
Yes Master?
You are not my master.  Damn this blindness. Is that you Imelda?
Oh...who is that? I do not recognise your voice. Damn this blindness.
Damn this blindness. Is that you Imelda?
Well obviously. Now, what do you want?

Not much. It is some ancient artifact that the Witch Lord is searching for. Other than that, there is little I can add. I have a talent with my hands though. If an item is placed in them, I can feel the powers within it. If I touch this Crown, doubtless I would be able to tell you more about it.
Who are you?
I am Largabo Branx. Clearly I don't know you.
I have always hated gnomes. You just can't trust them.
As a Cormaeril, you should know better than to judge on generalizations.
True enough I suppose.
That's pretty rich, coming from a Cormaeril!
What is it you want? Did the Witch Lord send you? Or was it Imelda?
Then why did you come? Does the Witch Lord know you are here?
Tell me what you want then.
Oh, I understand. I may be blind, but that doesn't make me stupid. The Witch Lord has not sent you, has he?
Easily enough. Just let me touch the objects you desire identified, and I will see what I can do.
Oh, I understand. I may be blind, but I am not stupid. You are not Imelda and the Witch Lord has not sent you, has he?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> What?
He must mean the Spell Mantle Cloak. A nice gift. Here you go.
A pair..of...
A suit of mail? I don't...
He must mean that old Ring of Change I guess. Here you go then.
Was there anything else?
If the Witch Lord is defeated then...does that mean...I am free?
Dead? Then you mean...I am free?
I am just a slave! Please, let me go!
Then I won't help you with it. Your loss.
What? I'll not go down without a fight...
But <FirstName>, it probably wasn't voluntarily. At least, I don't think so.
Well I do. Disgusting little wretch!
Oh...at last...
No. I may be blind, but I am familiar with the fort and the forest beyond, at least as far as Morfen. I will head there.
You'd free him? He's a servant of the Witch Lord. You should kill him!
A harsh judgement, Lady Kathryn.
So what does Imelda want?
I don't know what made you come to the fort. It's not like we haven't kept our end of the bargain.
To thank me? Well...I suppose it is good to be appreciated, though it's not as though I have any choice in what I do.
Hmmm... let me see...
Does the Witch Lord know you are here?
Money? Why would we pay...oh, I understand. You are not Imelda. Who are you really?
I'm leaving...
...that's everything I can tell you.
I have always hated the Witch Lord. Although I've never seen him, I could always feel his evil, and smell his evil. I just want to be free of him and this place.
The Witch Lord is a very fine master and...he treats me very well of course.

I am a secretary I suppose, if you can call it that. I look after the gold and belongings of the Witch Lord, or at least I account for them. I handle the pay of the troops and for our agents. The hogoblins cannot be trusted, and the Undead are not for this sort of task, so it is left to me.
I am done.
It's time for you to die.
Let's discuss something else.
What is it you do here?
<StartCheck>[Taunt]</Start> You're not a secretary. You're a slave more like.
<StartCheck>[Persuade]</Start> I bet there are a few secrets you could tell me about the Witch Lord, eh?
I want something from you, slave.
Why do you think I am your master?
Master? I am not your master.
Are you blind?
No.
I have decided what to do with you.
More to the point, who are you?
I am <FullName>.
Neither.
He knows.
I want to ask you some questions.
What can you tell me about something called the Wyvern Crown?
<StartCheck>[Persuade]</Start> He has commanded you to give me something.
He has rewarded me with a cloak.
He said you should give me a pair of boots.
He said something about a suit of mail.
He mentioned a ring you were to give me.
Thanks
I am done.
I have already defeated the Witch Lord. I can go where I like.
The Witch Lord is dead.
Can you identify some equipment for me?
Free? After serving the Witch Lord?
It's time for you to die.
<StartAction>[Attack]</Start>
You'll have to answer some questions first.
You are free to go.
Goodbye.
Just get out of my sight.
Do you need help getting out of the fort?
I don't trust you that far.
The Witch Lord sent me.
I have come on behalf of Imelda.
It is.
She just wanted to thank you.
I have nothing to do with Imelda.
Yes I know. I just wanted to thank you.
I have come for more money.
<StartAction>[Let the gnome try and identify your equipment.]</Start>
What bargain?
Thanks. I have no more questions for now.
What can you tell me about the Witch Lord?
Hello <FirstName>
Can I come with you again? I feel useless without doing something...
Yes, what is it?
Our cause is for Cormyr. Cormanthyr is long gone, but the elves would not want the realm overrun by evil. If there's something useful here, I believe we can take it.
Then we're in agreement. Let's get looting!
Lady Kathryn, I'm surprised by you!
Well, Edgar, I am full of surprises. This old coin for example, I think came from your pocket...
Why... I... you really are full of surprises. I am not sure how your father would feel about some of them...
Well, come on then. Enough talk. Are we going to raid it?
The elves guarded their tombs often with magic. Isn't that how the ghazneths, that brought so much destruction to Cormyr, were released in the first place?
I don't know Lacinda. Maybe you're right.
Who cares about what you think anyway? No one trusts what a Cormaeril has to say.
Child, leave the decisions to your betters. <FirstName>, you make the choice.
But... are you serious <FirstName>? We have come so far together!
That is true. <CUSTOM1020>, we'll follow your lead on this.
This is an ancient tomb. I am guessing elven, not anything to do with what we have encountered so far.
Well this is a cold and unpleasant place.
This place could do with the touch of the Morninglord! A little cheer, some light... perhaps we should seek a bard for our adventures!
I am glad to be out of Thunderstone though, even so. I get stifled in our castle!
Father never lets me out.
In many ways it reminds me of my ancestral home in Suzail. That was a cold and loveless place... all hard stone and leaks in the roof. We never had enough money to fix it.
Now of course, I don't have such worries. King Azoun took that house along with any money we had left.
I am sure that it will all work out for the best though Lacinda. With your help now, it will soon be recognised you're no traitor.
You have a lot to learn about human nature, Godfroy. I expect what we do here to make no difference to anyone's opinion except mine, and that's the one that counts.

Well, this is a shock <FirstName>. I don't know what it is I've done, but I'd still like to help out! I'll stay in the Furniture's Fate in Thunderstone for as long as I can, in case you change your mind.
Well I am certain that people will soon realize they misjudged you.
And rightly so! The Cormearils have been treacherous once too often!

The King did you an injustice I would say. Law and order are important, especially in times like these, but you are only distantly related to the traitors in the Abraxus Affair. It must hurt to have been branded with their treachery.
Ha! Maybe the King did us a favor taking that house! I hated it, but the label that goes with it... that I never earned.
Well they say that some traits are hereditary. Let's just hope that treachery isn't one of them.
Well child, wisdom clearly hasn't passed from your father to you, so perhaps I haven't inherited treachery!
Well, kings are not infallible it's true, though King Azoun IV was amongst the best.
It's hard to imagine it was built by Cormyrians when you see it now filled with such evil.
King Galaghard must have built this place to keep evil at bay. All he achieved was to make them a new stronghold.
Was Galaghard evil then?
Then TO BATTLE!
I don't think he did it deliberately.
Well of course not! I know little of Galaghard, but we have him to be thankful for defeating the Witch Lords.
Him and the elves.
Isn't that Valetto Stoutbold? There, by the wagons.
I'm not sure. He has a hard edge to him that one.
He might, but then again, he might not.
I didn't think so, and besides, he will need to know the farms are destroyed. When he hears what happened he will be bound to help us!
We were also due to pay his rents. Perhaps he'll be more interested in that.
Oh come on, Jonas! In a time like this you think Valetto's going to ask us for money!
Don't you think he might help us? I think we should ask.
I'll have a go if you like...
Text: 에. 아마도. 자노스가 네 물건 좀 뒤져볼게. 감정할 수 있는 게 발견되면 말해주지. 충분하지?

TextEng: True enough.
Valetto owned our farms.
I have met him once, when our father first negotiated the rents on the farms. A friendly sort, but a hard bargainer.
This must be Hawklin's castle.
Sir Hawklin is one of the few nobles who has always treated me with respect. I think you will find him a fair man.
At last I feel like there is a chance for reprisals against Lena's killers, and our father's, <FirstName>.
I just hope that I'm right...
But before we go and talk to Sir Hawklin, let's first deal with our father's request to bury him in the cemetery.
Sir Gilbert Hawklin has a fine reputation. Let's hope he lives up to it.
General dialogue in underground caves, WC. XXX
Fine, what do you need?
Something lives in here, and it smells very bad.
Nothing good could smell that bad. I think we should be ready for danger.
Let's be ready, <FirstName>.
I have a tendency to agree with you on this one Godfroy. The memory it stirs is not a good one, though I can't think why.
Well let's take a look around, then get out quick before I faint.
This smell is familiar. Where have I smelt it?
I can't place it, but it smells like mold.
That rules out pirates or smugglers, but what could it be?
I can smell salt on the breeze. We must be approaching the lake.
The water is brackish in the lake, almost like seawater. That's why farms are not common on the lake shore.
As you wish, <FirstName>. Do you want anything else?
I even read there are sharks in the lake!
Well, I don't think we plan to go in there, so I'm sure they won't bother us.
I have read the same thing, but unless we are intending to swim, I think we are likely safe from them on this quest.

When we decided we had to move from the King's Forest, my mother thought we should become fishermen on the lake. Father and I thought it would be better to go with your family, <FirstName>, and continue farming.
It's what we knew best after all, so it didn't seem such a bad decision. Sometimes, I can't help regretting it.
But I suppose there is no use looking backwards now...

Don't regret it, Godfroy. You had no idea what would happen. I for one am proud of the efforts you are making now to stop such things happening again. I am certain that Torm is guiding your hand in this.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
No, it is not revenge I want, but to stop such a dreadful thing happening to others.
What sort?
Text: "알겠어. 어떤 종류의 강화 주문을 사용하길 원하나?"

TextEng: I once sailed on the lake with my cousin Ayesunder. It is not really such a big stretch of water, and it was always an embarrassment to him that he could never find the pirates on the lake.
I read somewhere there are sharks in the lake. I'm not sure I'd want to sail on it.
Where magic is concerned, you can never be sure of anything. Your cousin must have endured a lot of comments. Well I know how that can feel...
For a Cormaeril, it must be far harder, though yes, he has suffered a lot of criticism. People are always too quick to search for traitors these days and blame treachery for a lack of results.

Well I know that! But I suppose it is only to be expected. My extended family opposed the Royal Family once too often. I must pay for that. I only hope you do not become a victim of such mutterings, Edgar Truesilver.
And I hope you do not suffer much longer for the failings of your family, Lacinda.
I hope that too...
What an odd place.
And... oh... by Tyr... what a stench!
And... oh... Lord of Battles, what is that awful smell?
Is there something else, then?
And... oh... Sweet Lathander... what a stench!
Torm preserve us, but that is a very nasty smell!
I think it's coming from those toadstools there.
Careful on the bridge, it's slippery.
This bridge looks fairly recent. Some of the castle must have got filled with debris over the years and Wyvernvapor's trying to dig it out.
Oh! I really hate bats!
Somehow that doesn't surprise me.
Bats are harmless, Kathryn. You shouldn't believe all that superstition about them.
Anyway, don't fear, <FirstName> and I are with you.
I appreciate that Godfory.
And what is my target?
This is a strange place to leave a pair of mirrors.
These are clearly magic mirrors of some sort. I have heard of mirrors that don't reflect light, but reflect instead only magic.
I am not sure.
Since we don't know, why don't we take them just in case?
Whatever you think is best, <FirstName>.
Well the mirrors are large; small enough to carry, but not for any extended time. I am guessing these mirrors are used for something here in the castle.
Then we should take them.
The Keeper mentioned something about mirrors and beams involved in a puzzle. We should probably take these.
They're not much use. I can't even fix my hair with these!
I think they must be important, otherwise they would not just be left standing here.
Well I'm pretty useful with a weapon now. I've had to defend my home before. I just wish I could have been there this time...
So be it!
Well they look useless to me, but if you want to take them <FirstName>, go ahead.
These are not ordinary mirrors. Look, their surface is shiny but they don't reflect anything.
Let's take them. They must have a use.
Perhaps they are some leftover from older times?
I wonder what they're for?
I guess that must be the Mythallar.
We do not have the knowledge or the tools necessary to break a Mythallar. We must find out how it powers the castle, and break whatever channels its power.
This is not something that my sword or my faith can conquer. I hope you understand these things better than I, <FirstName>.
I suppose the answers must lie here somewhere within the castle.
The question is, how do we shut off the Mythallar's power? Clearly we can't just climb up and jam it with a stick. There must be another way.
Sure. What's it to be?
I just hope we can find it.
It's very pretty isn't it? Seems a shame to try and stop it working.
Oh child! Why can't you concentrate on the task in hand? It is for your father's good that we deal with this thing. Let us concentrate.
Well I expect there's some reason you came too, Lacinda. No doubt some dark, secret reason that only a Cormaeril would understand.

Child, I came for <FirstName>, and <he/she> knows it. I'm sure it makes you feel good to throw the past treacheries of my family at my feet, but your family is no more noble than mine, even if it enjoys higher favor.
I just said it was pretty, that's all.
You are right. I will concentrate on the task in hand.
Look at the state of this place! The water must come in here all the time!
I thought this place would be more... well magical, and less horrible. Why would a dragon want to live here?
I don't think I will even attempt to guess, Lady Kathryn. Dragons are not something I know that much about.
It does seem a pretty nasty place to live, doesn't it?
Because dragons live in the real world, child, not in fairy tales, and generally they are not the gentle, playful creatures you've read about in all of your books!
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
Although that wouldn't apply to Wyvernvapor; Mist Dragons are at home in water.
Although that wouldn't apply to Wyvernvapor; Mist Dragons are at home in water according to the scripts I have read about them.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
Oh it smells very bad in here...
Ugh! It's disgusting! What a stench!
Maybe this is where the dragon lives?
This chamber stinks and it's big enough to house the dragon, so I think it must be Wyvernvapor's lair. It looks like we're in luck though. The dragon is away. We should use our time wisely.
This chamber stinks and it's big enough to house the dragon, so I think it must be Wyvernvapor's lair. It looks like we're in luck though. The dragon is away. We should use our time wisely.
This castle is very odd. It may seem deserted, but I thought I saw something move up on the roof.
If you look up at the top of the keep, you can see a watermark. I think the top of the castle never gets totally submerged. It's possible something might live up there.
We should be on our guard.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack. Maybe we should look for somewhere safer to tie a horse than that hitching post.
If you look up at the top of the keep, you can see a watermark. I think the top of the castle never gets totally submerged. It's possible something might live up there.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack. Maybe we should look for somewhere safer to tie a horse than that hitching post.
I'm not sure. It's very difficult to see in this mist.
Look over there, on the other side of the chasm! There's a cave with some steps.
Though I don't see a way across this chasm.
We could possibly jump a horse across. There's room for a run-up.
I think we should stick to our mission though. After all the castle won't be in there.
I agree. We have a task that we should stick to.
The Mythallar might be though, or a secret way in.
Well, I suppose that is possible.
Maybe we could use a rope to get across? I have one in my pack.
It's not a bad idea if we want to get across.
If we want to get across, that might be a way.
But would that be safe? Maybe there's another way...
Perhaps it's a smuggler's den?
For once child, you might be right.
Well we've found the castle...
Now we must find the Mythallar.
I'm sure that the end of our troubles is not far away.
Now to find the dragon. Can you believe it? We're actually looking for a dragon! It's like those tales about dragons in the history books...
"Then Kathryn and <FirstName> approached the great castle..."
It is a nice picture Kathryn. I'll look forward to hearing the full version when you are done with it.
Your father enjoys his tales, though I haven't heard him tell one since the war.
No, a lot left our lives when my brothers were killed and Father lost his arm. It's rare for him to even smile these days.
Some of the troubles of the realm rest on his shoulders. Let us continue on now and see what we can do to lift them. Remember though, it is the Mythallar we seek, not the dragon.

Child, your imagination is running away again. Try to remember that dragons are dangerous and spiteful lizards, not tales from your childhood. In any event we are looking for the Mythallar, not the dragon.
Well actually I have head that Wyvernvapor is not a dangerous dragon.
Well I'm sure we'll find out soon enough.
This place is a charnel house!
Can I hear fighting? I think there's a battle going on inside!
There must be more of them about. I can't wait to kill a few. Lena's death needs to be paid for!
It's very strange. Edgar Truesilver has a fine reputation as a commander. He would have posted sentries outside the barrow, so the enemy must have come up behind him.
It's Jonas... he seems distant.
Very well.
It's nothing, just...
I wish you had come back sooner, <FirstName>.
I'm sure it wouldn't have made a difference, but it just feels like... things would have gone better. We would never have been forced to leave the King's Forest, then Lena would not have... died.
The Blight would still have come, whether <FirstName> was here or not, and though my parents' deaths hurt, I am sure that it was the will of Lathander.
You sound like your father, Godfroy. I don't think it was anyone's will that Lena or our father died, just the work of something evil.
Well we will do what we can so others don't have to share our pain.
I don't care about other people. I just want Lena to rest in peace.
Well, I'm sure Sir Hawklin will help us.
You sound like Godfroy. Vengeance is what I want, <FirstName>, and I expect Sir Hawklin to give it to us.
I'm sure it wouldn't have made a difference, but it just feels like... things would have gone better. We would never have been forced to leave the King's Forest, then Lena would not have... died.
Why don't you show me?
Text: 자노스는 원하는 대로 실력과 능력을 키울 거다.

TextEng: The Blight would still have come, whether <FirstName> was here or not, and though my parents' deaths hurt, I am sure that it was the will of Lathander.
You sound like your father, Godfroy. I don't think it was anyone's will that Lena or our father died, just the work of something evil.
Well we will do what we can so others don't have to share our pain.
I don't care about other people. I just want Lena to rest in peace.
Well, I'm sure Sir Hawklin will help us.
You sound like Godfroy. Vengeance is what I want, <FirstName>, and I expect Sir Hawklin to give it to us.
We should be nearly at the place Sir Hawklin told us about.
I'm sure there's nothing for us to worry about. If Sir Hawklin trusts the Forest Folk, then I'm sure we can.
Yeah, well Godfroy, on this I prefer to be cautious rather than walk into a trap.
I think we should be on our guard. There's lots said about the Forest Folk, and it's not all nice.
Fine <FirstName>, if you think that is a good idea.
Let's just hope there isn't a trap ahead, laid by this Manthis person.
I have heard many people moan about the prices in the Six Coffers Trading Coster, but they say you can't beat it for variety.
This is Thunderstone. I've heard the local commander here is a little bit rough with the laws, so we should be careful.
I had hoped the first time we visited Thunderstone would be to sell produce at the market. Instead we arrive almost penniless, but at least I have hope in my heart.
Let's go and find Sir Hawklin.
Well let's not forget we have our father's remains to bury, <FirstName>. We must respect his wishes.
I've never been here before, though this was meant to be our market for crops from the farm. Now...
Have heart Jonas. I'm sure everything will be fine. Sir Hawklin is supposed to be a good man.
I hope we don't have to rely on your positive attitude to get us by for too long Godfroy, that's all I can say.

I haven't been to Morfen before. I always meant to, but since the move from the King's Forest, I just never got around to it. I hear it's a pretty small place, though there is a smithy here. We might be able to purchase some supplies, even weaponry although theoretically we need a Charter.

I also know a few spells my father taught me. He was a priest of Lathander for a long time, and has been able to guide my faith even when no clergyman could be found. I think you'll find me a useful companion, if you'll take me?
What do you need?
There's an Alehouse here, and I think a shop too. Some old War Wizard retired here. Maybe that's how Morfen remains unaffected by the raids.
Well, in better times this would have been a place for an ale and a chance for us to catch up on old times, <FirstName>, but now vengeance is all I'm interested in.

I guess you've not been here for a while, have you? In Cormyr you can't carry weapons that are not Peacebonded without a Charter allowing you to do so. A woodaxe or a hunting bow are fine, but anything more is illegal.

You left for too long, <FirstName>. In Cormyr you can't carry weapons that are not Peacebonded without a Charter allowing you to do so. A woodaxe or a hunting bow are fine, but anything more used to mean trouble.
In this area they used to take Peacebonding very seriously. If anyone was seen without a Peacestring tied over their weapon, and was found without a Charter, they were arrested immediately.
But things changed when war started. Cormyr was in such desperate danger that we all carried weapons, and freely too. I doubt Peacebonding is as important as it used to be.
Hello <FirstName>. Shall we work together once more?

TextEng: Was there anything else?

I am the last Cormas, and if we should fail in this quest, I will forever be the last Cormas...
There's not really any more to tell. I told you that I live only because I was the one my father carried from the burning church.

My father had to give up the priesthood, so that he couldn't be found so easily again. My mother had already given up her titles. The Morninglord blessed them though after that. Martin Bleth never found them, and soon all the Bleths were exiled.
And life, though hard, was peaceful. We lived on the farm in the King's Forest right up until the war.
I'll wait as long as it takes to change your mind, <FirstName>, but please don't let it be long.
I am the last Cormas, <FirstName>. Did you know that? It is a sad thing to think of.
I had a brother and a sister. Both were killed, murdered actually, when I was young.

My parents thought they had escaped all the intrigue when they left Suzail, but my mother had long had another man courting her. He was a noble from the Bleth family, another very powerful noble family that fell from grace along with the Cormaerils over a plot to kill the King.
In those days they were a noble family in high favor. I guess though they had always had their links to the Fire Knives; the band of once-noble assassins who seek to de-stabilize Cormyr.

Martin Bleth his name was. When he discovered my mother had married my father, he sent men to seek out newly appointed priests. Dressed as bandits, they attacked several Lathander churches, hoping to kill my father and capture my mother.

In their first attack, they set on fire the church, burning down the house attached to it. My father was badly injured carrying me to safety. Both my brother and my sister burned to death. I don't remember my brother or sister, but I sometimes feel guilty that I was the one to survive. I wonder what they would be doing now?
I suppose.
Probably that is true. I try to make them proud. I hope I do.
Thank you <FirstName>. I really hope so. I try to make them proud.
It seems like I have known you for a lot longer than I really have, <FirstName>. I guess that is because in some ways you remind me of your father.
Praise Lathander! At last I can help!
It's easy to forget how little we know of each other. You know of course that my father was a priest of Lathander, but probably you did not know that my mother was a noble of the Emmarask family?
OK. I may have more to say later.
The Emmarask family have long put all their will into their political careers. You know, it sounds so stupid now, but before the war I suppose all this sort of thing mattered.
My father on the other hand was no one important, so when the Emmarasks saw that my mother had fallen in love with my father, they did all that they could to stop it.
I think they particularly objected that my father was a priest of Lathander. Though the Church of Lathander is a great civilizing power, it is true that its excesses can make others jealous.

And other noble families, seeing a way to embarrass the Emmarasks, started circulating rumors about my parents. My father, embarrassed by the dishonor being placed on my mother, moved to a small parish in the King's Forest. My mother followed him there, and out of the glare of political intrigue in Suzail, they married.
It sounds a happy story, though it was really only the start of their hardships. We can leave that tale for another time though.
Did you want anything else?
<FirstName>?
No..it's alright. Forget it.
Hmmm. It looks like you have enough help already. I'll try another route <FirstName>. We can always join up later.
Take a look at that! There... through the mist. Can you see that huge cave?
There's a portcullis at the top too. That solves the mystery of where the pirate ships get hidden I guess. Air must get trapped inside when the castle floods.
It's musty in here...
This is a resting place for the dead. I am not sure how I feel about raiding it.
Don't be such a bore, Godfroy. Anything that's still here is not going to be missed by the owner, is it?
I don't think that's really the point Lady Kathryn. How would you feel if someone raided your grave?
I wouldn't care. I'd be dead, wouldn't I?
Let's take a look around. Anything that's still in this tomb is clearly not needed by the owner now!
This area was a burial place for the elves in the days when Cormanthyr was an elven kingdom. I guess this must date from that time, in which case it must be ancient.
It looks largely undisturbed. Whoever dug their way in here took very little, or else time has hidden their tracks.

A group of exiled nobles who seek to overthrow the Royal family.

A group of exiled nobles who seek to overthrow the Royal family. It is likely that many of my kin have joined them too, much to my shame. The majority of my family were exiled for their part in the Abraxus Affair, a plot to kill King Azoun IV before the war.
Our neighbors the Sembians have long coveted some of Cormyr's lands. Agents and spies are common here in Thunderstone.

Alice is a strange woman with enough secrets to topple almost anyone, but she never acts on the information she has. She has a code of her own. She can be trusted to do the jobs no one else wants to do, and that makes her useful. It's best if we don't cross her but instead go after the real villains.
I am saddened that you ask for money, <FirstName>. I do not need you to keep silent anyway. There is no entrance to the castle, only an exit.
Yes, I saw your last ride and it was quite something. Reminded me of Giogi Wyvernspur's last joust. Very impressive!

Suffice to say you have convinced me of your worth, and I will most certainly take you and any companions on as squires. I can only apologize that I was not able to offer you squiredom without first forcing you to prove your worth.

Times are very hard. The raids out of Hullack Forest have us very stretched, and a combination of the war and all the piracy on Lake Wyvernwater has put such a strain on my finances that even taking on new squires has to be seriously considered.

Many grumble that Laheralson and the Purple Dragons should be doing more, but that is not my jurisdiction and there's nothing I can do it about it, especially while the Sembians watch our borders so avidly.
You have already done enough Sir Gilbert. I tell you again it is Valetto that is behind the piracy on the lake!

Then I guess that Alice Broadhand was commissioned for the job. Well, I suppose it is nice to know someone is looking, but the information is not really useful without more detail. You must have come to tell me for a reason.

You have said it before Imelda. I have to tell you that if it weren't for Valetto's loans, and the fact that he is the only ready buyer of my lands, I would have been bankrupted long ago. Your merchant rivalries should not blind you to the fact that he is on our side!
<FirstName>, let me introduce you to Imelda, my business partner. She heads our ivory imports. They are the constant target of piracy on the lake.

Well <FirstName>, the tournament is drawing to an end. Feel free to enjoy what is left of it, then come over to the castle where I shall give you your first task. We shall see what we can do about these raiders.
Could you doubt it! With riding like that only a fool would turn you down. You are a dark horse, <FirstName>, winning a tourney when no one knows of you!

Goodbye, <CUSTOM1021> <LastName> <CUSTOM1053>, my one hope!
I'm not interested in running errands.
That is a ridiculous request.
Goodbye.
I want to ask you something else.
You'll need to give me something in return.
Forget it then.
What gold have you got?
Where can I find the White Stag?
Get on with it.
Who won't?
Go on.
I am done.
I have brought you the hide of the White Stag, as you requested.
I want something in return.
It was nothing.
What is it you need?
Remind me, what was the favor you asked me for?
Tell me again, who was it that defaced my father's grave?
Let me ask you something else.
I remember now. Thanks
Where can I find this person?
Thanks. I'm done for now.
Where can I get a job in this town?
Can you tell me anything about Polter's Fort?
My thanks to you.
The White Stag?
My thanks to you.
My thanks to you.
Let me ask something else.
What is it?
Do you know who did it?
What will make it easier?
I'm not interested.
That scum will pay!
Thank you for telling me this.
No. I have better things to do with my time.
I've wasted enough time on you. Goodbye.
Where can I find this <CUSTOM1022>?
It's a deal.
Tell me who defaced the grave and I'll consider it.
<StartCheck>[Intimidate]</Start> You should be more worried about not telling me.
<StartCheck>[Persuade]</Start> I will protect you from any harm.
I'll see what I can do.
I've seen it.
Yes I do.
Tell me who you think did it anyway.
What is the favor?
No, I don't.
Let me ask you another question.
Fine. Goodbye for now.
ROOT of final dialogue - comments are here
I became trapped when I tried to solve the puzzle that protects the Crown.
Thank you <FirstName>. Now if you can only find a way to free me of this power that holds me...
I have heard many people moan about the prices in the Six Coffers Trading Coster, but they say you can't beat it for variety.
This is Thunderstone. I've heard the local commander here is a little bit rough with the laws, so we should be careful.
I had hoped the first time we visited Thunderstone would be to sell produce at the market. Instead we arrive almost penniless, but at least I have hope in my heart.
Let's go and find Sir Hawklin.
Well let's not forget we have our father's remains to bury, <FirstName>. We must respect his wishes.
I've never been here before, though this was meant to be our market for crops from the farm. Now...
I suppose at best it offers us a chance of revenge, <FirstName>. That's what I hope for at least.
Have heart Jonas. I'm sure everything will be fine. Sir Hawklin is supposed to be a good man.
I hope we don't have to rely on your positive attitude to get us by for too long Godfroy, that's all I can say.

I haven't been to Morfen before. I always meant to, but since the move from the King's Forest, I just never got around to it. I hear it's a pretty small place, though there is a smithy here. We might be able to purchase some supplies, even weaponry although theoretically we need a Charter.
He got that right at least! But the deviousness of it!
There's an Alehouse here, and I think a shop too. Some old War Wizard retired here. Maybe that's how Morfen remains unaffected by the raids.
Well, in better times this would have been a place for an ale and a chance for us to catch up on old times, <FirstName>, but now revenge is all I'm interested in.

I guess you've not been here for a while, have you? In Cormyr you can't carry weapons that are not Peacebonded without a Charter allowing you to do so. A woodaxe or a hunting bow are fine, but anything more is illegal.

You left for too long, <FirstName>. In Cormyr you can't carry weapons that are not Peacebonded without a Charter allowing you to do so. A woodaxe or a hunting bow are fine, but anything more used to mean trouble.
In this area they used to take Peacebonding very seriously. If anyone was seen without a Peacestring tied over their weapon, and was found without a Charter, they were arrested immediately.
But things changed when war started. Cormyr was in such desperate danger that we all carried weapons, and freely too. I doubt Peacebonding is as important as it used to be.
<StartHighlight>Jonas is currently unconscious and will likely die if he is not given aid very soon.</Start>
Text: <StartHighlight>자노스는 현재 의식이 없고, 도움을 받지 못하면 곧 죽을 것입니다.</Start>

TextEng: That... that was bad. You ever experienced that, <FirstName>? It felt like death...
Text: 흥. 네가 제대로 했다면 자노스가 이런 불쾌함을 겪지 않아도 됐을 텐데.

TextEng: Come on then, let's get on. I don't want to think too much about what just happened.
Not likely <FirstName>. I'm sticking with you.
Text: 여기 남아 있겠어. 가고 싶으면 가.

TextEng: Szass Morg, the Witch Lord, is not the only one of his kind. There are others, more powerful, like the Witch Duke.
You call yourself family? I'm disgusted by you...
Can we get a move on <FirstName>? Vengeance can't wait for ever.
Quickly <FirstName>! Back to the farms!
I am still trapped, <FirstName>. Please, find some way to free me!
Please <FirstName>! Will you help me?
Help me! Please! Help me! The pain!
<FirstName>? Oh thank <Deity>! Please, you must help me!
I... I... am trapped, and I can feel my strength fading! You must help me <FirstName>!
Please! We are family, <FirstName>. It wasn't me before, I was controlled by the Witch Lord.
By all the gods, it's your brother, <FirstName>!
That's cheerful news at this point.
Sweet Lathander! It's Jonas!
I truly don't know, <FirstName>. Maybe because I am trapped and dying I am no more use to him, or maybe he knows your only hope to get the Crown is by me telling you everything he has told me.
Because if you can free the way to the Crown, maybe he has a chance to get it.
Because he can't get it himself, <FirstName>. It's a deliberate ploy, but at the same time, what choice do we have if we are to secure the Crown?

To get across to the island in the center where the Crown rests, there are 4 giant columns that rise from the pit. To get the columns to rise, you need to place four gems in their correct pedestals. Each gem is found in a Gem Golem here in this barrow.
I put one of them in a pedestal already, <FirstName>, taken from the first golem that Szass Morg destroyed. It was doing so that froze me here.

He is still here somewhere, watching. Perhaps he is waiting for you to unlock the puzzle to the Wyvern Crown, but <FirstName>, getting the Crown is also your only hope. You are defenseless against his powers without it.
As I put the gem on the pedestal, the force held me here. Maybe I did something wrong, I don't know, but I can feel it draining me. Please do something, <FirstName>, and quickly!
Let's get going, <FirstName>.
Yes, what is it?
I'll have a go if you like...
Text: 에. 아마도. 자노스가 네 물건 좀 뒤져볼게. 감정할 수 있는 게 발견되면 말해주지. 충분하지?

TextEng: As if you could teach me, <FirstName>! Go on then, show me what it is you know and I don't!
Text: 자노스는 원하는 대로 실력과 능력을 키울 거다.

TextEng: Well, if you must, though I don't know who made you our leader...
What do you need?
As you like. Anything else?
You think I'd be any better at it, do you? I'm just going to bash them if you can't open them. Is there anything else?
Thank <Deity>, I was sick of sneaking about. Is there anything else?
I'll try <FirstName>, but remember I was never any good at Hide and Sneak when we were young. Is there anything else?

The puzzle that guards the Crown can only be unlocked by a knight of Cormyr. That is the safeguard on this barrow. The safeguard was not put here not by the Cormyrians themselves, but by the Witch Duke who built it, to stop any of the Witch Lords trying to take the Crown for themselves.
I will do. Is there anything else?
Well I would've thought two pairs of eyes are better than one, but alright. Is there anything else?
That's more like it! Is there anything else?
You're kidding me aren't you? You expect me to just stand idle when there are enemies to kill?
Oh alright <FirstName>, I know that look. Is there anything else?
Just tell me where you want me.
Just so long as there are still enemies standing by the time I get into the fight, I'm fine with that. Is there anything else?
Some sort of battle tactic is it? Your experience is going to be useful to us <FirstName>, I can tell. Is there anything else?
I'm at your side, <brother/sister>. Is there anything else?
Alright <FirstName>, I'll pick them off happily, just so long as they pay for my Lena. Is there anything else?

The Witch Duke knew that if he were to die, before he could rise again one of the Witch Lords might make a play for the Crown, so he placed this safeguard on the Wyvern Crown to protect it. No true knight of Cormyr would willingly unlock the Crown for a Witch Lord.
See the whites of their eyes, that sort of thing, right? Suits me. I want to see them going down. Is there anything else?
You probably know better on this, but don't think it gives you the right to boss me about. I'll train how I like. Was there anything else?
Yes?
Nothing bothering me <FirstName>. How about you? You OK?
Text: "다 완전 끝내줘. 더할 나위 없지. 뭐... 내가 엄청 부자에 글래머한 하플링 아가씨들 하렘에 둘러싸여 있으면 더 좋겠지만... 그건 당장은 안 되겠지, 하하하!"

TextEng: Well you'll manage, I'm sure. Was there anything else?
Was there anything else?
I'm fine <FirstName>. Bit thirsty, that's all.
I've got a few cuts and scrapes. Nothing to worry about.
Text: "프흣, 난 걱정 마. 그냥 긁힌 상처 몇 개야."

TextEng: Was there anything else?
I've been better. These wounds hurt, but I can probably manage.
Text: "아까 좀 엉망이 되긴 했지, 헤. 볼 것까지는 없어."

TextEng: Szass Morg believed that I, as a Cormyrian and a squire, might be enough, but when I tried to place the first piece of the puzzle, this power seized me and froze me here, and now I can feel it leeching my life away!
No, I'm in serious trouble here <FirstName>. Look at me!
Text: "그냥... 몇 군데 긁혔을 뿐이야, 별거 아냐." 그는 얼굴을 찡그리며 빈 팔로 배에서 솟는 심한 피를 틀어막으려 합니다.

TextEng: Are we out of healing, or do you have anything?
I thought the fact that I keep putting my arms out in front of me might have alerted you to the fact there is something wrong with my eyes. I can't see a thing.
Text: "괜찮을 거야, 아마. 근데 여기가 정말 어두운 건지... 내가 진짜 눈이 먼 건지 말해 줄래? 살짝 걱정돼서."

TextEng: I... I don't think so <FirstName>. I think I've been poisoned.
Text: "어이! 완전 멀쩡해-내 혈관을 타고 흐르는 불덩이만 빼면 말이지. 그건... 알아서 해결되겠지..."

TextEng: Well I'm sweating, there are spots all over my skin, and I'm about to be sick. If you think that sounds like I'm OK, then I guess we're not going to get very far.
Text: "피부에 이상한 반점이 좀 생긴 것만 빼면 나쁘지 않아. 이거... 안 좋은 건가?"

TextEng: If you've got something to cure me, you'd better use it. Else, we have no choice but to go on.
What do you mean, 'tell me about yourself'? I'm your brother. Are you saying you've forgotten everything about me?
Come on <FirstName>, get serious. We have things to do. Are you done wasting time?

Thank you. I mean it <FirstName>. I know we are family, but I don't know if I'd have done the same if you'd been acting as I have. The worst thing is that a small part of me knew what I was doing... but let's not dwell on it now. We have our vengance at hand and I have a score to settle with the Witch Lord.
Later <FirstName>. First revenge. It can't wait any longer.

Please, free me, <FirstName>, I beg you! Please! I must have my revenge for Lena's death. While I am trapped, you can remove the ring from my finger that the Witch Lord uses to control me, and throw it into the pit. Then I will be truly free to fight by your side. Even if we die here it is better that way!
<FirstName>?
It's not relevant now.
Isn't that Valetto Stoutbold? There, by the wagons.
I'm not sure. He has a hard edge to him that one.
He might, but then again, he might not.
I didn't think so, and besides, he will need to know the farms are destroyed. When he hears what happened he will be bound to help us!
We were also due to pay his rents. Perhaps he'll be more interested in that.
Oh come on, Jonas! In a time like this you think Valetto's going to ask us for money!
I agree. No need to call more trouble on our heads.
Don't you think he might help us? I think we should ask.
Will you help me <FirstName>?
True enough.
Valetto owned our farms.
I have met him once, when our father first negotiated the rents on the farms. A friendly sort, but a hard bargainer.
This must be Hawklin's castle.
Sir Hawklin is one of the few nobles who has always treated me with respect. I think you will find him a fair man.
I hope so...
At last I feel like there is a chance to even the score with Lena's killers, and our father's, <FirstName>.
I just hope it's true...
But before we go and talk to Sir Hawklin, let's first deal with our father's request to bury him in the cemetery.
Sir Gilbert Hawklin has a fine reputation. Let's hope he lives up to it.
Please <FirstName>! I'll tell you what I know, but don't take long! You may not trust me, but this force is killing me!
This place is a charnel house!
Can I hear fighting? I think there's a battle going on inside!
There must be more of them about. Let's hope so. I have a debt to repay on these scum on behalf of my Lena.
Come on, <FirstName>! Let's go hunt any other hobgoblins down!
It's very strange. Edgar Truesilver has a fine reputation as a commander. He would have posted sentries outside the barrow, so the enemy must have come up behind him.
I wish you had come back sooner, <FirstName>.
I'm sure it wouldn't have made a difference, but it just feels like... things would have gone better. We would never have been forced to leave the King's Forest, then Lena would not have... died.
The Blight would still have come, whether <FirstName> was here or not, and though my parents' deaths hurt, I am sure that it was the will of Lathander.
You sound like your father, Godfroy. I don't think it was anyone's will that Lena or our father died, just the work of something evil.
Well we will do what we can so others don't have to share our pain.
You must show forgiveness, <FirstName>. Despite everything he has done, it's not his fault. At least think on it.
I don't care about other people. I just want Lena back... or vengeance.
I'm glad, <FirstName>. Our father needs avenging too. Family should stick together...
Well, I'm sure Sir Hawklin will help us.
You sound like Godfroy. Revenge is what I want, <FirstName>, and I expect Sir Hawklin to give it to us.
We should be nearly at the place Sir Hawklin told us about.
I'm sure there's nothing for us to worry about. If Sir Hawklin trusts the Forest Folk, then I'm sure we can.
Yeah, well Godfroy, on this I prefer to be cautious rather than walk into a trap.
I think we should be on our guard. There's lots said about the Forest Folk, and it's not all nice.
Let's just hope there isn't a trap ahead, laid by this Manthis person.
Trust no one, <FirstName>. It's the best way.
What happened to you?
Why would the Witch Duke do that?
<StartAction>[Kill your brother while he's helpless.]</Start>
Let's just avoid him.
Let's go and find out.
Either way, we don't have any to give.
Valetto Stoutbold?
Well, thanks for the information.
The Witch Duke?
I had business of my own.
I came back as fast as I could when I heard of the war.
That's what I want too.
You'll feel differently in time.
What difference would it have made?
Good.
Do you think we should expect trouble?
Let's have a look around.
What happened to the Witch Lord's power over you?
Heard anything else about Morfen?
What's a Charter?
What is a Charter?
Tell me about Peacebonding.
Thanks.
I need your help Jonas. Come with me.
You should remain here until you recover fully. You are still weak.
How would that help him?
You're right. Let's go.
I need to discuss something.
What is wrong with you?
Why would I help you?
How do I reach the Wyvern Crown?
Where is the Witch Lord now?
I'm done.
With some training you could improve your skills. Let's take a moment to teach you some useful tricks.<StartHighlight>[Level Jonas]</Start>.
Dismount from your horse.
Mount up!
Let's discuss tactics.
Actually, let's leave it at that for now.
Let's discuss something else.
Leave the locks on doors and chests and so forth to me. OK?
Give me a hand with locks. Some of them are beyond me.
No.
Yes.
Stop sneaking. I need to know where you are so I don't hit you.
No.
Yes.
<StartAction>[Decide what to do with your brother Jonas.]</Start>
Stay stealthy, but only until the next fight.
Use creeping tactics when we see enemies.
No.
Yes.
Help me look around for things. I think I might be missing stuff.
No.
Yes.
Leave me to do the searching.
No.
Yes.
I need to ask more questions first.
Attack as soon as you see enemies.
No.
Yes.
No.
Yes.
Let's change the distance between us.
We're too close together. Keep a good distance from me. We'll be safer that way.
No.
I'll consider it.
Yes.
Don't crowd me, but be ready to come to my aid.
No.
Yes.
Get close and stay there.
No.
Yes.
Move to range.
No.
Yes.
Well, you're definitely better in hand-to-hand, so get in close to our enemies.
No.
Yes.
I want to discuss your training.
No, that's it for now.
Yes.
Let's talk.
Is everything OK?
I'm not feeling too good.
I'm fine thanks.
<StartAction>[Take the Witch Ring from your brother and cast it into the pit.]</Start>
I'll see if I have anything...
Tell me a little about yourself.
I'm done for now.
Agreed. We can talk later.
Not so fast.
We don't have time for this now.
What is it?
Never mind.
Do you think he might help us?
I...I...must kill you....
I can't score and talk! Go away!
Hello again.
Look, would you consider letting me join your party? It's just the castle is a bit stifling and father never really lets me out.
But father's not an idiot, he knows I'm too like him to take such a passive route. I'm sure that he will see sense and let me do what I can to help. So how about it?
No. Locking me in the castle would never change anything, so I have found my own ways into and out of Thunderstone when I need to. My life became more secretive, always dodging servants...
I expect I probably sound a little boring don't I, but I have my dark secrets too you know... I just don't think I'm ready to share them with you just now.
Did you want anything else?
<FirstName>?
Forget it. I wanted to say something, but actually it's not important.
Take a look at that! There... through the mist. Can you see that huge cave?
There's a portcullis at the top too. That solves the mystery of where the pirate ships get hidden I guess. Air must get trapped inside when the castle floods.
It's musty in here...
This is a resting place for the dead. I am not sure how I feel about raiding it.
Don't be such a bore, Godfroy. Anything that's still here is not going to be missed by the owner, is it?
Well, if you change your mind, I'd really like to join you and get out of this castle for a bit.
I don't think that's really the point Lady Kathryn. How would you feel if someone raided your grave?
I wouldn't care. I'd be dead, wouldn't I?
Let's take a look around. Anything that's still in this tomb is clearly not needed by the owner now!
And we need whatever we can find.
This area was a burial place for the elves in the days when Cormanthyr was an elven kingdom. I guess this must date from that time, in which case it must be ancient.
It looks largely undisturbed. Whoever dug their way in here took very little, or else time has hidden their tracks.
Our cause is for Cormyr. Cormanthyr is long gone, but the elves would not want the realm overrun by evil. If there's something useful here, I believe we can take it.
Then we're in agreement. Let's get looting!
Lady Kathryn, I'm surprised by you!
Well, Edgar, I am full of surprises. This old coin for example, I think came from your pocket...
Great! Let's get to work!
Why... I... you really are full of surprises. I am not sure how your father would feel about some of them...
Well, come on then. Enough talk. Are we going to raid it?
The elves guarded their tombs often with magic. Isn't that how the ghazneths, that brought so much destruction to Cormyr, were released in the first place?
Who cares about what you think anyway? No one trusts what a Cormaeril has to say.
Child, leave the decisions to your betters. <FirstName>, you make the choice.
That is true. <CUSTOM1020>, we'll follow your lead on this.
This is an ancient tomb. I am guessing elven, not anything to do with what we have encountered so far.
Well this is a cold and unpleasant place.
This place could do with the touch of the Morninglord! A little cheer, some light... perhaps we should seek a bard for our adventures!
I am glad to be out of Thunderstone though, even so. I get stifled in our castle!
Your party looks a bit crowded. I need a bit of space ...  ask me again when there are less of you, and then I'll be delighted to come.
Father never lets me out.
In many ways it reminds me of my ancestral home in Suzail. That was a cold and loveless place... all hard stone and leaks in the roof. We never had enough money to fix it.
Now of course, I don't have such worries. King Azoun took that house along with any money we had left.
I am sure that it will all work out for the best though Lacinda. With your help now, it will soon be recognised you're no traitor.
You have a lot to learn about human nature, Godfroy. I expect what we do here to make no difference to anyone's opinion except mine, and that's the one that counts.
Well I am certain that people will soon realise they misjudged you.
And rightly so! The Cormearils have been treacherous once too often!

The King did you an injustice I would say. Law and order are important, especially in times like these, but you are only distantly related to the traitors in the Abraxus Affair. It must hurt to have been branded with their treachery.
Ha! Maybe the King did us a favor taking that house! I hated it, but the label that goes with it... that I never earned.
Well they say that some traits are hereditary. Let's just hope that treachery isn't one of them.
Look, would you consider letting me join your party? It's just the castle is a bit stifling and father never really lets me out.
Well child, wisdom clearly hasn't passed from your father to you, so perhaps I haven't inherited treachery!
Well, kings are not infallible it's true, though King Azoun IV was amongst the best.
It's hard to imagine it was built by Cormyrians when you see it now filled with such evil.
King Galaghard must have built this place to keep evil at bay. All he achieved was to make them a new stronghold.
Was Galaghard evil then?
I don't think he did it deliberately.
Well of course not! I know little of Galaghard, but we have him to be thankful for defeating the Witch Lords.
Him and the elves.
General dialogue in underground caves, WC. XXX
Something lives in here, and it smells very bad.
And I am sure you can trust me more than that Cormaeril you have with you.
Nothing good could smell that bad. I think we should be ready for danger.
I have a tendency to agree with you on this one Godfroy. The memory it stirs is not a good one, though I can't think why.
Well let's take a look around, then get out quick before I faint.
I can't stand this for too long.
This smell is familiar. Where have I smelt it?
I can't place it, but it smells like mold.
That rules out pirates or smugglers, but what could it be?
I can smell salt on the breeze. We must be approaching the lake.
The water is brackish in the lake, almost like seawater. That's why farms are not common the lake shore.
I even read there are sharks in the lake!
Are we ready to join up once more?
But I guess we're not likely to go swimming.
I have read the same thing, but unless we are intending to swim, I think we are likely safe from them on this quest.

When we decided we had to move from the King's Forest, my mother thought we should become fishermen on the lake. Father and I thought it would be better to go with your family, <FirstName>, and continue farming.
It's what we knew best after all, so it didn't seem such a bad decision. Sometimes, I can't help regretting it.

Don't regret it, Godfroy. You had no idea what would happen. I for one am proud of the efforts you are making now to stop such things happening again. I am certain that Torm is guiding your hand in this.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
No, it is not revenge I want, but to stop such a dreadful thing happening to others.
I once sailed on the lake with my cousin Ayesunder. It is not really such a big stretch of water, and it was always an embarassment to him that he could never find the pirates on the lake.
I read somewhere there are sharks in the lake. I'm not sure I'd want to sail on it.
I see you've got that Cormaeril with you. Care to have someone more reliable in the team?
Where magic is concerned, you can never be sure of anything. Your cousin must have endured a lot of comments. Well I know how that can feel...
For a Cormaeril, it must be far harder, though yes, he has suffered a lot of criticism. People are always too quick to search for traitors these days, and blame treachery for a lack of results.

Well I know that! But I suppose it is only to be expected. My extended family opposed the Royal Family once too often. I must pay for that. I only hope you do not become a victim of such mutterings, Edgar Truesilver.
And I hope you do not suffer much longer for the failings of your family, Lacinda.
I hope that too...
What an odd place.
Torm preserve us, but that is a very nasty smell!
I think it's coming from those toadstools there.
And... oh... by Tyr... what a stench!
And... oh... Lord of Battles, what is that awful smell?
Yes, what is it?
And... oh... Sweet Lathander... what a stench!
I just wanted to hear your voice. I really hate bats! They scare me.
Don't worry, Lady Kathryn, bats are harmless and the least of our worries.
Er, thanks... I think, Edgar, though that didn't really make me feel much better!
I shall guard you Lady Kathryn, have no fear of that.
I can look after myself, thank you very much!
No offence intended Lady Kathryn. You have already shown us your skills.
Oh I'm sorry, Edgar! I didn't mean to sound unkind, you just sounded so stuffy!
I take my duties seriously... too seriously perhaps, but I know your father would never forgive me if I returned and you did not.
Somehow that doesn't surprise me.
No, you're not serious! Why would you want to get rid of me? I thought we were in this together?
Bats are harmless, Kathryn. You shouldn't believe all that superstition about them.
Anyway, don't fear, <FirstName> and I are with you.
I appreciate that Godfory.
This is a strange place to leave a pair of mirrors.
These are clearly magic mirrors of some sort. I have heard of mirrors that don't reflect light, but reflect instead only magic.
Well the mirrors are large; small enough to carry, but not for any extended time. I am guessing these mirrors are used for something here in the castle.
The Keeper mentioned something about mirrors and beams involved in a puzzle. We should probably take these.
They're not much use. I can't even fix my hair with these!
Though I guess that's not their real use!
I think they must be important, otherwise they would not just be left standing here.

I'm very good at getting into and out of places I shouldn't. Father keeps me mostly in the castle, so I have to be, so if you're looking for someone who's good with locks, sneaking around and generally going unnoticed, I can do that.
Of course! You had me worried there!
Well they look useless to me, but if you want to take them <FirstName>, go ahead.
These are not ordinary mirrors. Look, their surface is shiny but they don't reflect anything.
Let's take them. They must have a use.
Well they look useless to me, but if you want to take them <FirstName>, go ahead.
Perhaps they are some leftover from older times?
I guess that must be the Mythallar.
We do not have the knowledge or the tools necessary to break a Mythallar. We must find out how it powers the castle, and break whatever channels its power.
This is not something that my sword or my faith can conquer. I hope you understand these things better than I, <FirstName>.
I suppose the answers must lie here somewhere within the castle.
The question is, how do we shut off the Mythallar's power? Clearly we can't just climb up and stop it. There must be another way.
Well if you don't want me with you any more, <FirstName>, I suppose that's your choice. But please, think about it. I'll be at the castle if you change your mind.
We'll find it, I'm sure.
It's very pretty isn't it? Seems a shame to try and stop it working.
But I suppose that's what we must do...
Oh child! Why can't you concentrate on the task in hand? It is for your father's good that we deal with this thing. Let us concentrate.
Well I expect there's some reason you came too, Lacinda. No doubt some dark, secret reason that only a Cormaeril would understand.

Child, I came for <FirstName>, and <he/she> knows it. I'm sure it makes you feel good to throw the past treacheries of my family at my feet, but your family is no more noble than mine, even if it enjoys higher favor.
I just said it was pretty, that's all.
You are right. I will concentrate on the task in hand.
Look at the state of this place! The water must come in here all the time!
I thought this place would be more... well magical, and less horrible. Why would a dragon want to live here?
Then TO BATTLE!
What a dreadful place.
I don't think I will even attempt to guess, Lady Kathryn. Dragons are not something I know that much about.
It does seem a pretty nasty place to live, doesn't it?
Because dragons live in the real world, child, not in fairy tales, and generally they are not the gentle, playful creatures you've read about in all of your books!
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
Although that wouldn't apply to Wyvernvapor; Mist Dragons are at home in water.
Although that wouldn't apply to Wyvernvapor; Mist Dragons are at home in water according to the scripts I have read about them.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
Whew! What a smell!
I'll have a go if you like...
Text: 에. 아마도. 자노스가 네 물건 좀 뒤져볼게. 감정할 수 있는 게 발견되면 말해주지. 충분하지?

TextEng: Is that how bad dragons smell? I'm glad there's no one at home. It's overpowering!
Maybe this is where the dragon lives?
Yes but where is he?
This chamber stinks and it's big enough to house the dragon, so I think it must be Wyvernvapor's lair. It looks like we're in luck though. The dragon is away. We should use our time wisely.
This chamber stinks and it's big enough to house the dragon, so I think it must be Wyvernvapor's lair. It looks like we're in luck though. The dragon is away. We should use our time wisely.
This castle is very odd. It may seem deserted, but I thought I saw something move up on the roof.
If you look up at the top of the keep, you can see a watermark. I think the top of the castle never gets totally submerged. It's possible something might live up there.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack. Maybe we should look for somewhere safer to tie a horse than that hitching post.
I'm not sure. It's very difficult to see in this mist.
Fine, what do you need?
If you look up at the top of the keep, you can see a watermark. I think the top of the castle never gets totally submerged. It's possible something might live up there.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack. Maybe we should look for somewhere safer to tie a horse than that hitching post.
Look over there, on the other side of the chasm! There's a cave with some steps.
Though I don't see a way across this chasm.
We could possibly jump a horse across. There's room for a run-up.
It should be easy enough.
I think we should stick to our mission though. After all the castle won't be in there.
I agree. We have a task that we should stick to.
The Mythallar might be though, or a secret way in.
That suits me! Was there anything else?
Well, I suppose that is possible.
Maybe we could use a rope to get across? I have one in my pack.
It might be difficult though.
It's not a bad idea if we want to get across.
If we want to get across, that might be a way.
But would that be safe?
Perhaps it's a smuggler's den?
For once child, you might be right.
Well we've found the castle...
Now we must find the Mythallar.
Like what?
Text: "알겠어. 어떤 종류의 강화 주문을 사용하길 원하나?"

TextEng: I'm sure that the end of our troubles is not far away.
Now to find the dragon. Can you believe it? We're actually looking for a dragon! It's like those tales about dragons in the history books...
"Then Kathryn and <FirstName> approached the great castle... "
It is a nice picture Kathryn. I'll look forward to hearing the full version when you are done with it.
Your father enjoys his tales, though I haven't heard him tell one since the war.
No, a lot left our lives when my brothers were killed and Father lost his arm. It's rare for him to even smile these days.
Some of the troubles of the realm rest on his shoulders. Let us continue on now and see what we can do to lift them. Remember though, it is the Mythallar we seek, not the dragon.

Child, your imagination is running away again. Try to remember that dragons are dangerous and spiteful lizards, not tales from your childhood. In any event we are looking for the Mythallar, not the dragon.
Well actually I have head that Wyvernvapor is not a dangerous dragon.
Well I'm sure we'll find out soon enough.
Is there something else, then?
Look at this place!
Can I hear fighting? I think there's a battle going on inside!
There must be more of them about. Let's hope so. I have a debt to repay on these scum on behalf of my Lena.
It's very strange. Edgar Truesilver has a fine reputation as a commander. He would have posted sentries outside the barrow, so the enemy must have come up behind him.
We should be nearly at the place Sir Hawklin told us about.
I'm sure there's nothing for us to worry about. If Sir Hawklin trusts the Forest Folk, then I'm sure we can.
Yeah, well Godfroy, on this I prefer to be cautious than walk into a trap.
I think we should be on our guard. There's lots said about the Forest Folk, and it's not all nice.
Let's just hope there isn't a trap ahead, laid by this Manthis person.
I have heard many people moan about the prices in the Six Coffers Trading Coster, but they say you can't beat it for variety.
And what is my target?
Oh, did you come back for me, <FirstName>? Does his mean we will be together again?
Text: 자노스에게 다시 합류하자고 요청하러 온 거지?

TextEng: Oh... then I'll wait here in case you change your mind.
Text: 젠장! 그럼 네가 정신 차릴 때까지 여기 있겠어.

TextEng: <StartHighlight>Kathryn is currently unconscious and will likely die if he is not given aid very soon.</Start>
Text: <StartHighlight>자노스는 현재 의식이 없고, 도움을 받지 못하면 곧 죽을 것입니다.</Start>

TextEng: I... I thought I died! I am so glad I didn't!
Text: 흥. 네가 제대로 했다면 자노스가 이런 불쾌함을 겪지 않아도 됐을 텐데.

TextEng: But of course!
Yes, you're probably right.
Text: 여기 남아 있겠어. 가고 싶으면 가.

TextEng: Good <QuarterDay> <FullName>.
I thought you were my friend, but I've learnt my lesson now. Why don't you leave me alone?
Hello. I am Kathryn Hawklin. You're <FullName>, aren't you?
You are! I know it. Father took you on as a squire didn't he? He said you had put new hope in his heart. I bet that's why he had Owain's room prepared... it was probably for you!
So be it!

Owain, yes. He was my brother... but he was killed in the war. Father hasn't even been in his room, nor Giles's, for more than two years. You must be special if it's because of you he had the room prepared. I wonder if that means father is starting to feel better?
Oh how exciting it is to meet you! Father has said lots of nice things about you. He said you had put new hope in his heart. I bet that's why he had Owain's room prepared... it was probably for you!
I'm also training myself to be a ranger. It's difficult because it's so hard to get out, but I'm a good tracker and know some of the ways of the wild.
What is it you wish me to cast?
Very well.
Sounds good to me. What can you show me?
Text: 자노스는 원하는 대로 실력과 능력을 키울 거다.

TextEng: Fine <FirstName>, just don't look too closely! You might see something that you don't think I should have!
OK. What do you want to change?
So can I come with you?
How?
As you wish. Is there anything else?
You think you're better than me at that sort of thing do you <FirstName>? I think you're wrong, but I'll do it. Was there anything else?
You don't need to ask me twice. I'm a professional at that sort of thing. Is there anything else?
Easy enough. Is there anything else?
Now you're talking! I can see you understand what I do best. Was there anything else you needed?
Did you think I wasn't looking? Oh..I see, you mean REALLY search. No problem. Was there anything else?
Well it goes against my nature, but I suppose I can stop for a bit. Is there anything else?
Is there any other way? Of course I will! Anything else you need?
You're the boss. I can do that. Anything else?
Well obviously I am Sir Gilbert's daughter and so I have been brought up to fight and look after myself. I may only be young, but I am a quick learner, and dying to get out of this castle.
Afraid I might get too close and pinch something from you?
Oh, you're too trusting, <FirstName>! Is there anything else?
Easy enough. Is there anything else?
Well that seems sensible. What should I be concentrating on do you think?
I've always been good at sneaking about and opening things I shouldn't, so that's what I'm concentrating on at the moment!
I figured I could do with improving my wilderness skills, so I'm a better Ranger, so that's what I'm doing at the moment.
I'm doing a bit of everything at the moment.
OK, no problem! Was there anything else on tactics?
Yes?
I'm fine thanks <FirstName>.
Text: "다 완전 끝내줘. 더할 나위 없지. 뭐... 내가 엄청 부자에 글래머한 하플링 아가씨들 하렘에 둘러싸여 있으면 더 좋겠지만... 그건 당장은 안 되겠지, 하하하!"

TextEng: But that's not my only reason. I can't just sit by and watch while my father's fortunes tumble. We stand to lose everything that we have left if we can't tackle the raids and who's behind them.
Did you need anything else?
Actually I'm feeling pretty good. I just wish I had a comb handy.
Did you need anything else?
I have a few scratches and cuts. I think father would be proud of me.
Text: "프흣, 난 걱정 마. 그냥 긁힌 상처 몇 개야."

TextEng: Although I'd like it if you could heal the one on my face, I don't want a scar.
I've felt a lot better. Some of these wounds are a bit painful.
Text: "아까 좀 엉망이 되긴 했지, 헤. 볼 것까지는 없어."

TextEng: <FirstName>, do I actually look alright to you? Heal me would you, I've got wounds all over.
Text: "그냥... 몇 군데 긁혔을 뿐이야, 별거 아냐." 그는 얼굴을 찡그리며 빈 팔로 배에서 솟는 심한 피를 틀어막으려 합니다.

TextEng: Or shall we just talk while I bleed to death?
I can't see anything by Tyr! It's terrifying.
Text: "괜찮을 거야, 아마. 근데 여기가 정말 어두운 건지... 내가 진짜 눈이 먼 건지 말해 줄래? 살짝 걱정돼서."

TextEng: Is there anything you can do to help?
I just need a chance to help my father and do whatever I can.
I can't say I've been on many adventures, but is it normal for wounds to make you feel like there's fire running through you? And my hands keep cramping too. Oh, and my chest hurts as well.
Text: "어이! 완전 멀쩡해-내 혈관을 타고 흐르는 불덩이만 빼면 말이지. 그건... 알아서 해결되겠지..."

TextEng: Actually I feel really ill. I think I must have caught some sort of disease.
Text: "피부에 이상한 반점이 좀 생긴 것만 빼면 나쁘지 않아. 이거... 안 좋은 건가?"

TextEng: If you've got anything to help me feel better, that would be good.
I don't have anything else to say just now. Perhaps later.
I was talking about Effie before, wasn't I? Oh, we had such fun together <FirstName>.  Even after what happened, I still miss her.

We had a fight one day, a silly fight. Effie said I was about as quiet as an ox when I was trying to creep about, and I got mad at her. She challenged me: if I thought I was so brilliant, to try and steal some papers from Hurim Thiodor's office.

I didn't attempt it. I knew Hurim has eyes like a hawk, and besides, most of the stuff in the Crown Office is warded by the War Wizards, so I thought that wasn't a fair challenge. I was upset though, so I thought if I could steal something from Effie herself, then she'd realise I was a better thief than she was.

So that's what I did. It was quite easy really. I jostled her next time we were at the market, and dipped my hand into her pocket. I didn't come away with much, just a tiny piece of parchment, rolled up like it was from a carrier pigeon. I laughed at her and held up the parchment for her to see it.

She tried to snatch it back, but I held her away at arm's reach and had a quick look at it. It just had some name on it, and a tiny little symbol of a dagger wreathed in flames. I didn't think it was important until I saw Effie's reaction. Her face had gone all white. I got a bit scared then and just gave the paper back. Effie took it and walked off. I never saw her again.
Because that parchment revealed her for who she was.
If you give me the opportunity to come with you, you won't regret it.

The name was Admiral Ayesunder Truesilver, Edgar's cousin. He'd been due into Thunderstone just a few days later. I'd always liked Edgar, as he was nice to me even when I was a child. I think it was that which made me keep thinking about the parchment.
The name was Admiral Ayesunder Truesilver, Edgar's cousin. He'd been due into Thunderstone just a few days later.
The Truesilvers have ever been high on the Fire Knives' list. I should know that.
You were always nice to me when I was a child, Edgar. I think it was that which made me keep thinking about the parchment.

I asked my father what the little symbol meant. I was sure I'd heard of it, but I couldn't remember where. Father got very frightened. He pressed me to tell me where I'd seen it, and when I told him, he was so shocked he had to sit down.

I'd been a total idiot, <FirstName>. The little symbol was the symbol of the Fire Knives, a group of assassins dedicated to murdering the nobility of Cormyr. Effie had been slowly training me, so I could steal for them, or maybe even to recruit me. With Effie revealed as an agent, she'd made a run for it. Worse, I'd put my own life in serious danger.
So that's why my father has kept me under such close watch. The Fire Knives for certain will come for me one day, but what could I do? Stay inside forever?
I'm a noble, as good a target as any. Who knows, maybe Effie was disgraced by her discovery and I'm top of the list?
Anyway, I suppose there's no point worrying about that now, is there. Was there something else you wanted?
The symbol, <FirstName>. One that as troubled my life too.

He can't keep me locked up forever, and he knows it. I think he'd rather he let me out his way; through formal dinners, banquets and so forth. He probably thinks he should try to find me a husband too, one that can look after me.
I told you how it was difficult to get out of the castle after the war. Father was over-protective of me, and always worried about my ability to get into trouble...
Sometimes I wish I had listened to him more, but the truth is, I could hardly be expected to stay cooped up forever, could I?

Truth is, I rebelled a bit <FirstName>. I was only sixteen after all, and I hated been stuck indoors. I had a very good friend, Effie her name was, and she was always doing exciting things. Sometimes when I escaped from the castle, we'd go to the market together. Effie was such fun, and so daring. Sometimes she'd pick the pockets of the nobles...
