Effie taught me a lot of things. She was a master of creeping about silently too, and of picking locks and stuff like that. I always thought it was just for fun, and it turned out I was pretty good at it too.
...  but it wasn't long before it got me in trouble ...  I think though that I'd rather keep that story to myself.
Well I've had a very protected life. During the war I had to stay at home with my mother and help to run things. I was too young to ride with my father and brothers.
OK. I may have more to say later.
I wish I could have gone, though my father always tells me how glad he is I didn't. Both of my brothers were killed in one of the battles by Arabel, and my father lost his arm...
When my mother heard the news, she just sort of faded away, until... she died...
Father came back of course, but he's not the same man. He always seems sad. He's so afraid of losing me too, that for the last few months he has barely let me leave the castle.
Do you have any skills I could use?
Not just now thanks.
Eagle's Splendor.
Divine Favor
Death ward.
Cure Moderate Wounds
Cure Minor Wounds
Cure Light Wounds
I've changed my mind. Let's discuss something else.
Cast on all the party members.
Cast it on <CUSTOM77102>.
Cast it on <CUSTOM77101>.
Certainly. Come with me.
Bless.
Aid.
With some training you could improve your skills. Let's take a moment to teach you some useful tricks.<StartHighlight>[Level Kathryn]</Start>.
Dismount from your horse.
Mount up!
Let's discuss tactics.
Actually, let's leave it at that for now.
Let's discuss something else.
You need to look after me better.
Heal me only if I'm seriously wounded.
Heal me when I'm moderately wounded.
Heal me even when I'm only slightly wounded.
No.
Yes.
Leave the locks on doors and chests and so forth to me. OK?
No.
Yes.
Give me a hand with locks. Some of them are beyond me.
No.
Yes.
Stop sneaking. I need to know where you are so I don't hit you.
No.
Yes.
Use a stealthy approach until the next fight.
Use creeping tactics when we see enemies.
No.
Yes.
Help me look around for things. I think I might be missing stuff.
No.
Yes.
You're slowing us down, stop searching and sneaking.
No.
Yes.
I'm done.
Attack as soon as you see enemies.
No.
Yes.
No.
Yes.
Let's change the distance between us.
We're too close together. Keep a good distance from me. We'll be safer that way.
Don't crowd me, but be ready to come to my aid.
Get close and stay there.
Thank you for your help, but now it is time we parted company.
No.
Yes.
Move to range.
Well, you're definitely better in hand-to-hand, so get in close to our enemies.
No.
Yes.
I want to discuss your training.
<StartAction>Kathryn will train as she sees fit.</Start>
<StartAction>Kathryn will level up as a Rogue only</Start>
Actually no, stay with me for a while longer.
<StartAction>Kathryn will level up as a Ranger only.</Start>
Good. I think we are done for the moment.
Yes.
Let's talk.
Is everything OK?
Let me see what I have...
Tell me a little more about yourself.
It sounds like you don't see her any more.
So what did happen?
I'll bet you got caught, didn't you?
So what did you get?
Nevertheless, that is my decision.
You tried to steal something form Hurim Thiodor? That's a disgrace!
Go on.
Why did Effie get so upset?
Whose name was on the parchment?
What was so important about the parchment?
You think they will come after you, even now?
I'm done, thanks.
That's right.
It sounds like you got yourself into trouble though.
Absolutely not. It was unfair to keep you locked up!
Stop there. We can talk more later.
I'm done for now.
That was probably a good thing.
I can see his reasons. Maybe it was the right thing to do?
And?
I'm done for now.
Let's discuss something else.
We don't have time for this now.
What is it?
I want you to use your magic.
I don't want you to cast any spells until I say otherwise.
Text: "내가 달리 말하기 전까지는 주문을 사용하지 마."

TextEng: I want you to go ahead and cast spells on your own.
I need you to cast a group of buffing spells.
Never mind.
No, nothing else.
Why would that be useful?
Can you tell me what they might be for?
Yes.
Cast all the buffing spells you have.
Lacinda, you still have to prove yourself.
Kathryn, stop being stupid and stick to our quest.
Cast all the buffing spells that last a long time.
Must you do this now?
That is enough. I trust you both. Let's concentrate on the Mythallar.
Cast all the short duration buffing spells.
You're imagining things.
I've changed my mind.
What did you see?
Cast on all the party members.
Cast it on my animal companion.
Cast it on my familiar.
Good.
Do you think we should expect trouble?
Tell me a little about yourself.
Cast it on me.
I have still need of your help. Travel with me once more.
You should remain here until you recover fully. You are yet weak.
Cast it on yourself.
I might be
No
Did you want something?
Owain?
Yes
Never mind.
Spell resistance.
Restoration.
Shield of faith.
Remove diesease.
Neutralize poison.
Lesser restoration.
How will your father feel?
Invisibility sphere.
Greater santuary.
Greater restoration.
Greater undead.
Freedom of movement.
Entropic shield.
Never mind.
Yes?

Well of course! The Wyvern Crown used to belong to the Witch Lords hundreds of years ago, and this was their castle. Of course the Witch Lords were defeated by Cormyr, and the Royal Family had the crown for ages, but it was stolen and then lost.
GUARDIANS
I prefer to talk about the Mythallar, but go ahead.

The keys for the portal are the same keystones that are needed to unlock the crystal ball. Oh, I think I said that already didn't I? Each is guarded by a Guardian. Well, Master calls them the Guardians, but they're not all alive.

There's the wyverns that have one keystone, one is in that weird place behind the old chapel and one Guardian is an infernal puzzle. The Master thought that was the best way to keep them safe. Frankly if I had them spread around like that I'd just forget where I put them, but I guess the Master knows best.
Oh I'm not interested in that sort of thing! Something to do with beams and mirrors and doors. Some of it's flooded too, just makes it harder according to my Master.

If you interested in looking at it, you'll have to go to the level below though. Watch out down there. The Master has coerced some troglodytes into clearing some of the old passageways. The Master's trying to find something. Those trogs are nasty little blighters, and tame or not they have an evil nature.

Some leftover from when the Witch Lords had this castle I think. There's a sort of door in the chapel, but it goes into this musty cave that doesn't fit the dimensions of the castle. Isn't that a fascinating concept? I wonder if that is linked to the Mythallar? I must look that up...
Where was I? Oh yes, don't know much about what's in that room, though it smells bad in there. Did I mention that?

The wyverns? Well of course you must have seen them? They live on the roof of the castle mostly. Not very pleasant creatures I would say, but the Master keeps them under control. Probably the keystone is in their nest or whatever it is they live in. Just the smell keeps everyone away!
BALL & PINNACLE
No. My Master has made me go through the old library and I have given him every book that mentions it. I think my Master is worried about the Wyvern Crown, though I don't know why.
Well I don't know much about it, but go ahead.

Well one of the pirate captains did tell me something about it after some drunken pirates got killed going through the portal...let me see...one came back didn't he? Kept saying something about "the blades let you come back, but they don't let you go forward!" Kept screeching it apparently until everyone decided he was quite mad.

But maybe he was mad before, since he took a horse with him through the portal. Or was that another time? No, I don't remember. I'm not really interested in that. I could tell you a bit about the Mythallar though, if you like? Or did I already do that?

You need the keystones to get through the portal. Not long ago some of the pirates went through the portal while drunk, and several of them were killed by whatever was on the other side. The Master decided to lock the portal so that it couldn't be used unless he desired it.

The keystones are ancient keys used by the Netherese to lock the crystal ball to the pedestal and keep it safe. The Master decided to use the same keystones to lock the portal. Then he gave the keystones to the Guardians so that the crystal ball would be safe, from drunken pirates or anyone else.
It's a tiny island out on the lake. You can't reach it from the sea, only from the sky or through the portal of course here in the castle.

In most respects it's like a normal magic item, except the Netherese made many items that required the power of Mythallars to work. The ball is like that. The magic of the ball detects the weather on the lake, but the magic doesn't work if the link to the Mythallar is broken.

The ball sits on the Pinnacle on a pedestal, testing the weather. The pedestal is the link. If the ball is removed the castle sinks. If the ball is destroyed the castle will sink forever. Can you imagine that? No one would be able to study the Mythallar then. How terrible would that be?
Mythallar
What is it?

I look after the Mythallar, though of course I know little about it. I think the Master lets me stay just to humor me. I'm sure one as wise as he knows all there is to know about the Mythallar, but...a kindness to me, I believe it is.
I don't think so. Perhaps with very powerful magic. Of course the Mythallar is just a power source. It doesn't do anything without the crystal ball.
But then why would someone want to destroy the Mythallar? It's such a beautiful thing.
You're teasing me I know it! Everyone knows it's the Mythallar that makes the castle rise and fall out of the lake. I guess you must be new here.
A Mythallar really is nothing more than a source of power, although the secret of how the Netherese built them is lost. Imagine if we knew, eh? That was always my dream....where was I?

Oh yes...power. Well yes, you see, the Mythallar here in the castle can power magic items - not real ones of course, but special ones within range of the Mythallar. There's one in the foundations somewhere that makes the castle rise and fall, and another that detects the fog on the lake.

Well, I can't pretend I really know that. I mean the detail, you know? Only the Master does, but...the crystal ball on the Pinnacle of course detects the weather. I think I mentioned that didn't I? The ball does the detecting and the Mythallar provides the power to make the castle move. The ball doesn't work if it's not on its pedestal of course, because then the link to the Mythallar is broken and the castle sinks back into the lake.
Go ahead...
Ah yes! You again...er...yes. The name will come to me again in a moment I'm sure.
Now don't forget, the Master has the south and east ways to the Mythallar trapped. One of these days I'm gonna forget. What a way to go eh?!
Well, hello...er...I'm sorry, I've forgotten your name.

Course, there was a time when I didn't live here...oh, many years ago now. I was studying in the hope of becoming a War Wizard and I just got fascinated with all things Netherese. I came here to find the Mythallar. Did I say that?
Well, then welcome.
Come to look at the Mythallar have you? Amazing isn't it? The Netherese were astonishing I think...don't you?
This! This beautiful magic...thing! It's Netherese you know, or did I already say that?

Well, I just never got around to leaving. The Mythallar is so fascinating and the Master so accommodating...well, perhaps you'd like to talk a bit about the Mythallar? You pirates so rarely talk to me...
Oh...I do beg your pardon. I thought you must be one of the pirates...who did you say you were?
Oh...Ha, ha...ye you tricked me there...anyway, where were we?
Well, I suppose it's none of my business who visits the Master. How can I help you?
Well...I am...my, I've forgotten my name. Isn't that funny? Most people just call me the Keeper. I've got so used to it I've forgotten my real one.
Goodbye for now.
Do you know anything about something called the Wyvern Crown?
Who are you?
<StartAction>[Ask something about the guardians.]</Start>
Where can I find the keys to the portal?
Tell me about the puzzle.
Tell me about the weird room.
Tell me about the wyverns.
<StartAction>[Ask something about the crystal ball.]</Start>
Do you know where it is now?
Any idea what's on the other side of the portal?
How do I get through the portal to the Pinnacle?
Where is this Pinnacle where the crystal ball is?
How does the crystal ball work?
<StartAction>[Ask something about the Mythallar.]</Start>
Let's change the subject.
Can the Mythallar be destroyed?
What are you doing here?
What does this Mythallar do?
How does the Mythallar make the castle rise or fall?
Goodbye.
<StartAction>[Talk about something else.]</Start>
I am <FullName>.
You never knew it.
What's a Mythallar?
What are you talking about?
Pirates?
A friend of the Master.
I am a pirate really.
I didn't.
The Hawklin girl must die!
Slay me Kathryn Hawklin!
Kill the Cormyrian dogs!
ROOT of general questions.

When I watched you riding in the joust, I saw the person that I wish I had become. I admire you <FullName>. I can't fully explain it, but it seems to me you have all the trappings of the knight I once wished to be.
I am honored, <FullName>.

I can't see, <FirstName>. It's not the first time; if you play around with magic, it can happen; but that doesn't make it any less frightening. I'll go on if we have to, but do you have anything to cure me?
Text: "괜찮을 거야, 아마. 근데 여기가 정말 어두운 건지... 내가 진짜 눈이 먼 건지 말해 줄래? 살짝 걱정돼서."

TextEng: I've played with enough potions to know when I've been poisoned. I hope you have an antidote.
Text: "어이! 완전 멀쩡해-내 혈관을 타고 흐르는 불덩이만 빼면 말이지. 그건... 알아서 해결되겠지..."

TextEng: If you don't, then there's nothing I can do except carry on.
There's something wrong with me <FirstName>. I can't stop itching, and I'm feeling sick. I must have caught a disease. Do you have anything?
Text: "피부에 이상한 반점이 좀 생긴 것만 빼면 나쁘지 않아. 이거... 안 좋은 건가?"

TextEng: I don't have anything else to say just now. Perhaps later.

I told you how knighthood was closed to me, and the hopes of fame and chivalry soon faded as I realised what they were; a fool's dreams. There was no time for bitterness. I could find no way to support myself, and no one to employ me even if I had had any skill worth using. By necessity I fell to theft, I soon lost my pride, and some would say I lost my dignity.

I could not have been further from the King's eye, or so I thought. What possible threat could I be? But wily Vangerderhast, the Court Wizard, was always on the watch for trouble, and seeing what had become of me, saw a risk that desperation might make me turn on the Crown.

It was actually he that set me on the path of the Arcane Arts. He gave me a tutor to set me on my course. But he gave with one hand, and took with the other, closing the door to the War Wizards, so I would never gain any power at court.
His eyes, or the eyes of his followers must have always been on me... must be on me still I guess. I can only hope this quest will finally prove my loyalty to Cormyr.
Do you think that is fair, <FirstName>?
Your party looks big enough already, but come back if you have need of me in the future.
I value your views <FirstName>, even when they are not the same as mine. I admire you, it is true. I could say that my loyalty to you is stronger even than my loyalty to Cormyr.
It goes beyond even the chance of redemption that you have given me. I will follow you wherever you lead.
I... I don't know. Would you ask it?
I am glad then <FirstName>, for I would hate to have to choose between you and Cormyr. I might be forced... I don't know. Forget it.
Then I hope that day will never come, for I think I would choose you before Cormyr.
I... I think I have talked enough for now on this subject.
It is true, <FirstName>... but you have heard enough of my story.

I will share a little more detail with you now, <FirstName>. All you have heard is the family history that everyone knows and judges me by. Many even say I was lucky to escape with so light a punishment. All we lost was our family seat in Suzail, and I hated that place anyway.
But the truth is, the day the King spared us from exile was not the day my troubles ended. I am grateful to him for his mercy, but the fall was still a hard one.
OK. I may have more to say later.
Hello to you.

Since my family's fall, I have not been able to pursue any career that looks like a threat to the King. All the doors once open, are now closed. Positions of any power are gone, but the one that hurt me the most was the pursuit of physical prowess. You may not think to look at me now, but I was a promising warrior before our fall.

Knighthood was my goal, the same as you have now achieved. I dreamt of glory in the jousts, my name known across the lands for my skill and my chivalry. When the fall came, it was rare to find a tourney I could enter, and when I did, I was pelted with offal, even stones, so that my horse would become skittish and I would be forced to withdraw.
Treachery caused that, <FirstName>, not mine, but others'. I hate traitors to Cormyr with a passion.
Perhaps, <FirstName>, perhaps. In weak moments I wish the King had left us more. But in his place I would not have been kinder.
They have been years of hardship since, but now there is hope in my heart. Let's not talk anymore of my past.
I don't know, <FirstName>. My head says the King's justice on all the Cormaeril's was necessary. Our family had been treacherous once too often.

My heart just feels the pain of what I have lost because of that treachery. I hate those involved in it with a passion. Some think my loyalty to Cormyr is questionable. If anything it is stronger, because what I lost was caused by traitors.

It is still early in our friendship for me to talk freely, <FirstName>. My story is an unhappy one for me, and often misunderstood by others. I would prefer it if we knew each other better before I share detail.
That might be best. I may have more to say later.
I'll tell you what is already common knowledge <FirstName>, before you hear it from another...
I am busy right now, maybe we can talk later, unless you intend to enter the joust?

My family are traitors to Cormyr, <FirstName>. Not my immediate family, but the Cormaerils in general. Once too often we have opposed the crown. Our latest attempt was not long ago; an elaborate poisoning attempt on King Azoun IV before the war.

I was not involved in the plot. I am from a distant and unimportant branch in the Cormaerils. That didn't save us completely from the King's justice, though we escaped exile. Our punishment was to lose our ancestral lands, though the King left us with something.
So that is my story as everyone knows it. Judge as you like.
I'm glad to hear that. Perhaps there is more I will be willing to share, but not just now.
Was there anything else you wanted?
That is a shame <FirstName>. I am enjoying doing something meaningful for once, something more... knightly, as I have craved for much of my life. Let me stay.
I am glad. You won't regret your choice...
As you wish. I shall pass by The Sign of Thunder from time to time. I would be pleased if you change your mind. Seek me out there if you do.
I see. It looks like I was a fool to believe in you. You are just another brainless dolt, falling for rumor and hearsay. I don't need you to help you!
<FirstName>?
Well if you are, I would like someone to ride for me. If you can persuade me you are worthy, then I would lend you my horse for the jousting.
I had something to say, but it's not important now.
Take a look at that! There... through the mist. Can you see that huge cave?
There's a portcullis at the top too. That solves the mystery of where the pirate ships get hidden I guess. Air must get trapped inside when the castle floods.
It's musty in here...
This is a resting place for the dead. I am not sure how I feel about raiding it.
Don't be such a bore, Godfroy. Anything that's still here is not going to be missed by the owner, is it?
I don't think that's really the point Lady Kathryn. How would you feel if someone raided your grave?
I wouldn't care. I'd be dead, wouldn't I?
Let's take a look around. Anything that's still in this tomb is clearly not needed by the owner now!
This area was a burial place for the elves in the days when Cormanthyr was an elven kingdom. I guess this must date from that time, in which case it must be ancient.
As you like.
It looks largely undisturbed. Whoever dug their way in here took very little, or else time has hidden their tracks.
Our cause is for Cormyr. Cormanthyr is long gone, but the elves would not want the realm overrun by evil. If there's something useful here, I believe we can take it.
Then we're in agreement. Let's get looting!
Lady Kathryn, I'm surprised by you!
Well, Edgar, I am full of surprises. This old coin for example, I think came from your pocket...
Why... I... you really are full of surprises. I am not sure how your father would feel about some of them...
Well, come on then. Enough talk. Are we going to raid it?
The elves guarded their tombs often with magic. Isn't that how the ghazneths, that brought so much destruction to Cormyr, were released in the first place?
We should be cautious.
Who cares about what you think anyway? No one trusts what a Cormaeril has to say.
In what way?
Child, leave the decisions to your betters. <FirstName>, you make the choice.
That is true. <CUSTOM1020>, we'll follow your lead on this.
This is an ancient tomb. I am guessing elven, not anything to do with what we have encountered so far.
Well this is a cold and unpleasant place.
This place could do with the touch of the Morninglord! A little cheer, some light... perhaps we should seek a bard for our adventures!
In many ways it reminds me of my ancestral home in Suzail. That was a cold and loveless place... all hard stone and leaks in the roof. We never had enough money to fix it.
Now of course, I don't have such worries. King Azoun took that house along with any money we had left.
I am sure that it will all work out for the best though Lacinda. With your help now, it will soon be recognised you're no traitor.
You have a lot to learn about human nature, Godfroy. I expect what we do here to make no difference to anyone's opinion except mine, and that's the one that counts.
Well I am certain that people will soon realise they misjudged you.

I am seeking someone to ride on my behalf. It has fallen out of fashion these days, but it used to be common for ladies, or even for lords, to pick a champion to ride for them in the joust. It is only a sign of prestige or honor. It will cost you nothing.
And rightly so! The Cormearils have been treacherous once too often!

The King did you an injustice I would say. Law and order are important, especially in times like these, but you are only distantly related to the traitors in the Abraxus Affair. It must hurt to have been branded with their treachery.
Ha! Maybe the King did us a favor taking that house! I hated it ...  but the label that goes with it? That I never earned.
Well they say that some traits are hereditary. Let's just hope that treachery isn't one of them.
Well child, wisdom clearly hasn't passed from your father to you, so perhaps I haven't inherited treachery!
Well, kings are not infallible it's true, though King Azoun IV was amongst the best.
It's hard to imagine it was built by Cormyrians when you see it now filled with such evil.
King Galaghard must have built this place to keep evil at bay. All he achieved was to make them a new stronghold.
Then cleaning it out is best thing we can do!
Was Galaghard evil then?
Not so fast. I can tell you are down on your luck. Would you bring me honor riding in the joust, or would you go out in the first round?
I don't think he did it deliberately.
Well of course not! I know little of Galaghard, but we have him to be thankful for defeating the Witch Lords.
Him and the elves.
This is Hawklin's castle in front of us.
Sir Hawklin is one of the few nobles who has always treated me with respect. I think you will find him a fair man.
At last I feel like there is a chance for revenge for Lena's murder, and for that of our father, <FirstName>.
But before we go and talk to Sir Hawklin, let's first deal with our father's request to bury him in the cemetery.
Sir Gilbert Hawklin has a fine reputation. Let's hope he lives up to it.
General dialogue in underground caves, WC. XXX
Something lives in here, and it smells very bad.
Well expectations are not enough for me. I shall seek another knight. It might be you are capable of riding on my behalf in the future, but I think I'll wait and see you ride in a joust first.
Nothing good could smell that bad. I think we should be ready for danger.
Sensible words.
I have a tendency to agree with you on this one Godfroy. The memory it stirs is not a good one, though I can't think why.
Well let's take a look around, then get out quick before I faint.
Agreed.
This smell is familiar. Where have I smelt it?
I can't place it, but it smells like mold.
Well mold can't harm us.
That rules out pirates or smugglers, but what could it be?
I can smell salt on the breeze. We must be approaching the lake.
I have asked around about you, and it seems you have a quest and a determination... I would like to be part of it; to help in something of value after all these years. Will you take me with you?
I can see you are not a worthy knight for me. Good day to you, <mister/missus>.
The water is brackish in the lake, almost like seawater. That's why farms are not common on the lake shore.
I even read there are sharks in the lake!
I have read the same thing, but unless we are intending to swim, I think we are likely safe from them on this quest.

When we decided we had to move from the King's Forest, my mother thought we should become fishermen on the lake. Father and I thought it would be better to go with your family, <FirstName>, and continue farming.
It's what we knew best after all, so it didn't seem such a bad decision. Sometimes, I can't help regretting it.

Don't regret it, Godfroy. You had no idea what would happen. I for one am proud of the efforts you are making now to stop such things happening again. I am certain that Torm is guiding your hand in this.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
Well, revenge will make you feel better, I'm sure.
No, it is not revenge I want, but to stop such a dreadful thing happening to others.
I once sailed on the lake with my cousin Ayesunder. It is not really such a big stretch of water, and it was always an embarassment to him that he could never find the pirates on the lake.
You always say I'm the one with the temper <FirstName>, but I think we'd do better not to make enemies so early on.
I read somewhere there are sharks in the lake. I'm not sure I'd want to sail on it.
Where magic is concerned, you can never be sure of anything. Your cousin must have endured a lot of comments. Well I know how that can feel...
For a Cormaeril, it must be far harder, though yes, he has suffered a lot of criticism. People are always too quick to search for traitors these days, and blame treachery for a lack of results.

Well I know that! But I suppose it is only to be expected. My extended family opposed the Royal Family once too often. I must pay for that. I only hope you do not become a victim of such mutterings, Edgar Truesilver.
And I hope you do not suffer much longer for the failings of your family, Lacinda.
I hope that too...
What an odd place.
And... oh... by Tyr... what a stench!
And... oh... Lord of Battles, what is that awful smell?
And... oh... Sweet Lathander... what a stench!
If we are to be squires, I think we will have to behave better to the ladies, <FirstName>.
Torm preserve us, but that is a very nasty smell!
I think it's coming from those toadstools there.
Careful on the bridge, it's slippery.
This bridge looks fairly recent. Some of the castle must have got filled with debris over the years and Wyvernvapor's trying to dig it out.
Oh! I really hate bats!
Somehow that doesn't surprise me.
Bats are harmless, Kathryn. You shouldn't believe all that superstition about them.
Anyway, don't fear, <FirstName> and I are with you.
I appreciate that Godfory.
This is a strange place to leave a pair of mirrors.
I'll gain even less if my champion winds up on <his/her> back in the first pass!
These are clearly magic mirrors of some sort. I have heard of mirrors that don't reflect light, but reflect instead only magic.
Well the mirrors are large; small enough to carry, but not for any extended time. I am guessing these mirrors are used for something here in the castle.
The Keeper mentioned something about mirrors and beams involved in a puzzle. We should probably take these.
They're not much use. I can't even fix my hair with these!
I think they must be important, otherwise they would not just be left standing here.
Well they look useless to me, but if you want to take them <FirstName>, go ahead.
These are not ordinary mirrors. Look, their surface is shiny but they don't reflect anything.
Let's take them. They must have a use.
Perhaps they are some leftover from older times?
I guess that must be the Mythallar.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Well, yes, I suppose that is true... then ride for me!
We do not have the knowledge or the tools necessary to break a Mythallar. We must find out how it powers the castle, and break whatever channels its power.
This is not something that my sword or my faith can conquer. I hope you understand these things better than I, <FirstName>.
I suppose the answers must lie here somewhere within the castle.
The question is, how do we shut off the Mythallar's power? Clearly we can't just climb up and stop it. There must be another way.
It's very pretty isn't it? Seems a shame to try and stop it working.
Oh child! Why can't you concentrate on the task in hand? It is for your father's good that we deal with this thing. Let us concentrate.
Well I expect there's some reason you came too, Lacinda. No doubt some dark, secret reason that only a Cormaeril would understand.

Child, I came for <FirstName>, and <he/she> knows it. I'm sure it makes you feel good to throw the past treacheries of my family at my feet, but your family is no more noble than mine, even if it enjoys higher favor.
I just said it was pretty, that's all.
You are right. I will concentrate on the task in hand.
Here, take this as a token of my favor. You can wear it on your glove. And here, this fine horse in the scale barding is mine. You will find him temperamental, but an excellent warhorse.
Look at the state of this place! The water must come in here all the time!
I thought this place would be more... well magical, and less horrible. Why would a dragon want to live here?
I don't think I will even attempt to guess, Lady Kathryn. Dragons are not something I know that much about.
It does seem a pretty nasty place to live, doesn't it?
Because dragons live in the real world, child, not in fairy tales, and generally they are not the gentle, playful creatures you've read about in all of your books!
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
Although that wouldn't apply to Wyvernvapor; Mist Dragons are at home in water according to the scripts I have read about them.
Hopefully, we won't run into him though.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
If anyone is going to live in here, there must be a system of watertight doors, otherwise they'd all drown.
Good luck in the joust <FullName>. I shall be watching your progress with interest!
This chamber stinks and it's big enough to house the dragon, so I think it must be Wyvernvapor's lair. It looks like we're in luck though. The dragon is away. We should use our time wisely.
This castle is very odd. It may seem deserted, but I thought I saw something move up on the roof.
If you look up at the top of the keep, you can see a watermark. I think the top of the castle never gets totally submerged. It's possible something might live up there.
We should be on our guard.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack. Maybe we should look for somewhere safer to tie a horse than that hitching post.
If you look up at the top of the keep, you can see a watermark. I think the top of the castle never gets totally submerged. It's possible something might live up there.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack.
We must be on our guard. If something is on the roof, it's a good vantage point from which to attack. Maybe we should look for somewhere safer to tie a horse than that hitching post.
I'm not sure. It's very difficult to see in this mist.
Look over there, on the other side of the chasm! There's a cave with some steps.
Possibly that's true, but that doesn't make you a good rider.
Though I don't see a way across this chasm.
We could possibly jump a horse across. There's room for a run-up.
I think we should stick to our mission though. After all the castle won't be in there.
I agree. We have a task that we should stick to.
The Mythallar might be though, or a secret way in.
Well, I suppose that is possible.
Maybe we could use a rope to get across? I have one in my pack.
It's not a bad idea if we want to get across.
If we want to get across, that might be a way.
But would that be safe?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Yes, you look it. Very well then...
Perhaps it's a smuggler's den?
For once child, you might be right.
Well we've found the castle...

Now we must find the Mythallar. I'm not certain finding a way to shut this thing down will be easy. The Netherese didn't make control of Mythallars so easily available, at least from everything I have read.
I just wish I remembered more...
I'm sure your knowledge will be valuable to us, Lacinda.
Your faith in me is quite flattering, Edgar. Unfortunately it is probably misplaced.
I'm sure that the end of our troubles is not far away.
Now to find the dragon. Can you believe it? We're actually looking for a dragon! It's like those tales about dragons in the history books...
"Then Kathryn and <FirstName> approached the great castle... "
Well, you don't look like the sort who's been in many jousts...
It is a nice picture Kathryn. I'll look forward to hearing the full version when you are done with it.
Your father enjoys his tales, though I haven't heard him tell one since the war.
No, a lot left our lives when my brothers were killed and Father lost his arm. It's rare for him to even smile these days.
Some of the troubles of the realm rest on his shoulders. Let us continue on now and see what we can do to lift them. Remember though, it is the Mythallar we seek, not the dragon.

Child, your imagination is running away again. Try to remember that dragons are dangerous and spiteful lizards, not tales from your childhood. In any event we are looking for the Mythallar, not the dragon.
Well actually I have head that Wyvernvapor is not a dangerous dragon.
Well I'm sure we'll find out soon enough.
This place is a charnel house!
Can I hear fighting? I think there's a battle going on inside!
There must be more of them about. I can't wait to kill a few. Lena's death needs to be paid for!

For a Cormaeril to take up arms is frowned upon, even in these difficult times, so I have spent my time pursuing other skills. In hard times I have had to rely on subtlety, even theft I'm ashamed to admit.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Really? Well in that case I'm glad I approached you.
They must be inside the barrow.
It's very strange. Edgar Truesilver has a fine reputation as a commander. He would have posted sentries outside the barrow, so the enemy must have come up behind him.
We should be nearly at the place Sir Hawklin told us about.
I'm sure there's nothing for us to worry about. If Sir Hawklin trusts the Forest Folk, then I'm sure we can.
I hope you're right.
Yeah, well Godfroy, on this I prefer to be cautious rather than walk into a trap.
I think we should be on our guard. There's lots said about the Forest Folk, and it's not all nice.
Though gossip is not something you should always believe. I should know that.
Let's just hope there isn't a trap ahead, laid by this Manthis person.
The Six Coffers Trading Coster is the main merchant's Coster in Thunderstone.
Well... my name is Lacinda Cormaeril...

I have heard many people moan about the prices in the Six Coffers Trading Coster, but you can't beat it for variety. Magurk's might serve us better for everyday equipping, but if we need something special, we may have more luck here.
Are we ready to journey together once more?
Text: 자노스에게 다시 합류하자고 요청하러 온 거지?

TextEng: Fine, if that is what you wish I shall remain here in the hope that you change your mind.
Text: 젠장! 그럼 네가 정신 차릴 때까지 여기 있겠어.

TextEng: <StartHighlight>Lacinda is currently unconscious and will likely die if he is not given aid very soon.</Start>
Text: <StartHighlight>자노스는 현재 의식이 없고, 도움을 받지 못하면 곧 죽을 것입니다.</Start>

TextEng: Sometimes sorcery and magic can take us close to the realm of death, but that was the real thing, I am sure of it. This must be your doing, <FirstName>. My thanks.
Text: 흥. 네가 제대로 했다면 자노스가 이런 불쾌함을 겪지 않아도 됐을 텐데.

TextEng: Very well. I will come with you once again.
I shall stay then. Journey well.
Text: 여기 남아 있겠어. 가고 싶으면 가.

TextEng: Good <QuarterDay> <FullName>.
I do not wish to speak to you. Go away.
So, <FullName>, I am impressed! Truly you did ride well as my champion.
I see that name does not register with you.
I am very grateful to you for the honor you brought me.
I am very grateful to you for the honor you brought me.
I shall be in the Sign of Thunder. Pass by sometime. I think you and I might be able to work together.
Thank you. You may keep the horse, you have earned it.

Very well. It will cost you a donation of 150 golden lions to the shrine. I will attempt to remove all unnatural ailments that I can from you and any companions, although I cannot guarantee that it will remove whatever ails you.
Certainly disease is a foul affliction, but not the domain of Tempus. If you wish to be healed, you must donate 100 golden lions to the shrine and I shall attempt to cure you and any companions.
Those look like the wounds of battle, and fairly taken. Tempus welcomes your courage.
Ask what you need.
Of course. What are you looking for?

One-armed Magurk's is the place for the best prices and also where most Adventurers go. He's low on stock since the war, but still the best place in town. You'll find his place just north of the square next to the livery.
Magurk's place backs on to the Six Coffers Trading Coster, the main merchant trader's house in Thunderstone. They have everything, but are more expensive.
Most certainly.
Tournaments run in the fields to the east of town.
Sir Hawklin's castle is at the south end of Thunderstone. You can't miss it, it's a big stone structure.
It's at the south end of town.
The Furniture's Fate is probably the most appropriate for you, on the east side of the square next to Wangle's Livery.
I recommend the Sign of Thunder for someone of your stature. It's opposite our shrine.

But of course my child! Tempus as I am sure you know is the God of War. The Church of Tempus is charged with keeping warfare a thing of rules: preventing the slaying of innocents, and punishing the unjust or the cowardly. Here in Thunderstone there is much work, for many beasts still come from the Hullack Forest; cowardly slayers of innocent farmers.
What more do you need to know?
Polter's Fort? Well there's a name I have not heard for a while, but I can certainly share a story or two.

You know the fort itself was never called Polter's Fort? It was originally named Galaghard's Fort, after the king who started building it. After his defeat of the Witch Lords, about 400 years ago, Galaghard started the fort as a way to keep better control over eastern Cormyr. It was never finished though.

There was an even older foundation at Polter's Fort, and the builders dug something up while building the keep. Legends tell us it was some fearful beast that ate workers each night, but those legends are untrue; the nature of the creature lies in the nickname of the fort: Polter's Fort. It comes from Poltergeist's Fort you see.
From the store? Or maybe you would like a blessing for your father's grave? I hear that it was recently defaced.

The Poltergeist is a particularly restless spirit, and had they had a priest present with the know-how, they could have laid it to rest easily enough. However the fear spread through the fort, and it was deserted. Very few would venture near it after that, so it seems the Crown gave up on it.
Since then others have taken up living there from time to time, but never for long. So there it stands deep in the forest, almost complete yet completely deserted.

Commonly they are tortured spirits that make their presence felt in a semi-malevolent fashion. Often they throw objects, or even use weapons, but what drives them is their continuing torment, not a need to do evil.
Almost certainly. If for some reason you are thinking of venturing to Polter's Fort, then you must take with you the method to lay this spirit to rest.
Well, it is true that I have such a thing in my possession, though I don't know who told you.
I bought it at the market, though that is actually not your business.

Unicorns are creatures of great magical powers and some of those powers reside in the horn after their deaths. It is said that the horn of a unicorn is a powerful ingredient when crafting magic items, particularly weapons.

The Shrine of Tempus here in Thunderstone is a humble place, but it is still my duty to serve Tempus in every way that I can. Fine weapons are the friend of true warriors. It is my hope to craft such a weapon and dedicate it to Tempus, the Lord of Battles, so that one day a worthy hero can wield it.
Alas! That might be so, but it will be a long time before this church can afford to actually make the weapon.
No. Tempus is guiding my hand in this I am sure.

I have tried to find out, but with no luck. If you haven't spoken to Jenny Drabb, you should try and find her, as she is in the Garden a lot. She might know something. She does the laundry for the Furniture's Fate, among other places, so you might find her there.

<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Hmmm. Perhaps I might at that...

That is acceptable.
That is acceptable.

Certainly. I can perform a blessing on the grave from the Shrine of Tempus. For a fallen warrior such as your father, those that approach the grave will feel some of the awe he commanded in life. It should offer some protection so that the grave is not vandalized again.
Hmm. You have strength it seems...
You are a worthy foe, but not such a test that I could not easily overcome you...
Enough! I shall not surrender the horn to you, though I admit my respect for you has grown. Let us forget about the horn.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start>Very well. You are a worthy opponent. The horn is yours...
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Stolen you say? Well, I don't want to get into trouble for having something that is not rightfully mine, so I will return it to you...
Here you go, the horn is now yours. If you wanted the horn for your own uses, you should take it over to the smith in Wangle's Livery. She is new, but has a reputation for fine craftsmanship.
Was there anything else?
Then goodbye for now, and the Lord of Battles keep you.
You can make a fine weapon with a unicorn's horn. I had assumed that's why you wanted it.
Certainly, one moment while I prepare it....
I ask only for a donation of twenty-five golden lions in return, to further the work of Tempus.
You will need to sprinkle the Holy Water over the spirit. You cannot just throw the water wholesale and hope, you have to sprinkle it, which means you must first subdue the spirit.
That will depend on the nature of the Poltergeist, so you will have to use your wits.
I am indeed very pleased to hear that. This spirit deserved to be released after so long. Tell me, was there any physical form left?
Ah well, sometimes the items left behind are quite useful.
Well perhaps you should take it over to the smith in Wangle's Livery if you kept it. Sometimes such old blades can be reforged into a new weapon. Yes, I think Tempus would be pleased by that!
Welcome, stranger, to the shrine of Tempus here in Thunderstone. The Lord of Battles welcomes you to his church, even if you are not of the faith.
My name is Magnus. You may seek me out any time you need help, especially if you have battles or trials that have caused you to take wounds.
I shall pass by after the next prayers and bless the grave. Tempus shall watch over your father's body. He was a warrior after all. Was there anything else?
What kind of aid do you need?
A travesty! There is nothing that the Lord of Battles hates more than a cursed weapon or item!
Good <quarterday> to you Magnus.

I remember you. <CUSTOM1021> <FirstName> <CUSTOM1053>, they call you.

Anyway, we got wind of an ambush, bandits riding down on us, so we all hid in the coffins. Problem was, I couldn't fit, so I had to get one of my fellas to cut my arm off. It was that or certain death.
When the bandits saw all the blood around the wagon, they figured another group had already dealt with us and had taken anything worth having!

A group of kobolds it was. Nasty little creatures, but we never took'em seriously 'till that day. Decided we wanted the gems from the eyes of some statue they were worshipping. Easy job, quickly kill the high priest, hack out those gems and away.
Before we knew it we were surrounded by forty of the little devils. I got netted, and while I was struggling to get free, one of the little scumbags had my arm off with his cleaver!
More than you know, <lad/lass>! Now, what are you gonna buy?
Ah that's a tale to tell, but a lengthy one, but the long n' short of it is, I got a big swing and don't know my own strength.
Well I was out logging on Thunderstone Peaks, found me a piece o' timber, a real beauty it was! Took aim with my axe, and missed... the timber that is!
That's an understatement <Sir/Madam>, that timber was worth a fortune, and me bleeding all over it like a stuck pig! Now you want to buy, or just pass the time o' day asking questions?
Here you go then.
Well certainly. I've got a load of new stock in. Every time I look at the weapons though it reminds me how I lost my arm.
What do you need?
Want to hear the tale?
Yes, of course you have! Well then...
Come on! You don't look like the sort for a regular job! You want to be an adventurer, that's what you want, like I was once.
Truth is, adventuring is expensive to get started in Cormyr, 'cos the Charter is so expensive, but you could always head for the Dalelands, get started there.

That old place? I went out there once when I was younger, with a band of fellas. Place was empty, at least the keep was. We didn't go too deep though. I cut my hand on an old piece of metal and the infection got so bad they had to take my arm off.
Well my arm has come off in stages, that's the truth of it. Now stop askin' difficult questions and buy something.
Suit yourself then.
I see you're making a name for yourself. You'll be wanting the equipment to match your reputation!
Welcome <Sir/Madam>! I've got the finest goods this side o' Thunderstone. Magurk is my name, how may I help you?
You can ask, can't guarantee I got the answer though.

I reckon I know you well enough now <FirstName>. The truth is I lost my arm fair and square in some unimportant battle in some long forgotten little backwater. There's no romance or glamour in it, and probably only I remember the battle. That was the end of my adventuring days, though I was on no adventure.
Ha! I've got that covered too. Now come on, I've only got one arm and there's more than one customer in here. You looking to buy, or are you just looking?
I was on the King's crusade against the Tuigan Horde. I'm only glad that I lost my arm in the service of Cormyr, and not because of my own greed, though every day I curse the man who took it.
Well, that's enough on the subject. Are you going to buy anything?
Now that's a tale of bravery and romance. How I got my wife you know, though she's dead now, Lathander bless her memory. She was already betrothed to me, but was stolen by slavers.
Well I followed her to a distant land across the seas, through storms and pirate attacks, right to the port of the slavers...

I stole her back the moment she was off the auction block. Gave her new 'master' a smack on the head right in the middle of the market place, and just threw her over my shoulder. Course I got caught. They accused me of theft, and the penalty was my arm. Could have got even worse, but the judge was so stirred by my tale, that he let us both go free.
I was doing a spot of adventuring down by Hultail in those days. I don't remember why, but for some reason some fellas and I were taking a cart full of empty coffins down to Wheloon.
You like a tall story, don't you?
I'm done for now.
I want to ask something else.
Let's see what you have to sell.
That must have hurt.
That's a bit embarassing.
Sure, show me what you have to offer.
Well, can I ask something else?
I am done.
I'd like to see what you have to sell.
Thanks.
No thanks.

Where can I get a job in this town?

My thanks to you.

I thought you said you lost your arm a different way?
No, I'm going now.
I want to ask you something.
What about the other side of Thunderstone?
I appreciate you telling me.
Hello again!

Certainly! I was given it by an adventurer some years ago in return for a favor I had done him. The treasure is still unclaimed as far as I know, mainly because it is guarded. Fighting is not my strength, else I'd go and take a look myself. I can sell you the map if you're interested?
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Well, I suppose I can knock five golden lions off the price ... call it <CUSTOM1008> golden lions.
Well dear, we're not exactly rich either you know. Besides, I've had to listen to Mander go on about that map for years. I think we deserve a fair price.
<StartAction>[Success]</Start> Well, I suppose I can knock five golden lions off the price ... call it <CUSTOM1008> golden lions.
You should be careful if you're thinking of trying to tackle it, dear. That creature became Curst as a result of stealing a magic sword. Doubtless it has the sword still.
Aye, the legend tells us he was once a ranger who stole a katana from the secret stash of a sorceror. She cursed him as a result. He's been lurking in the marshes ever since.
Come back to buy it have you?
Well there's not much point since you've already bought it!
Here you go! Spirits and ales and a little extra!
Or...maybe you'd be interested in this treasure map?
Well you seem a bit down on your luck. You should get yourself up to Thunderstone: the big news is about the tournament there. Plenty of opportunities for those on Tymora's good side.
You're not going on about that old map again, are you dear?
Sure.

Well, the knights will be jousting of course, but there's plenty of stuff to do for us common folk too; competitions, open market, opportunities to buy or sell, gossip to be had. It's the place to go!
What is it?
Hmmm...I see. Seems a shame to give Londro any more money. He just drinks it, but very well.
Was there anything else?
I think once is enough for this!

Dreadful! Dreadful to hear another such tale! They are far too common. Alas, there's no one in Morfen who can help you, unless...you could try Brondar, our resident wizard, but he alone would not be enough.
You're best off heading up to Thunderstone. The troops are stationed there. Nothing else I can tell you on that I'm afraid.
The trail will be cold before we get any help! How will I ever avenge Lena?
Welcome stranger. I am Mander and this is my alehouse!
And why not Mia? It's a genuine map. Why shouldn't I?
Well <FirstName>, we had some Hultail spirits if you are interested, though stock is dwindling...
Because like as not, it's the Curst that guards it, and this fine <man/woman> does not look up to fighting a Curst.
Well the Curst lives in the marsh where it comes close to the road to Thunderstone. That's local knowledge, and you can reach the marsh by following the stream where the road crosses it.
But without the map, you will only find the Curst, not the treasure. That's the point.
Hmm ... how about <CUSTOM1008> golden lions?
And here's your map. Just make sure you're ready in case the Curst is waiting for you.
Shame, but I can wait another year or two and see if someone else comes along!
Thanks for your time.
Tell me more about this treasure map.

<StartCheck>[Bluff]</Start> Ah well, I'm not interested then.

Good luck. We shall meet again. If you bring us some proof of having stopped the hunting, before our next meeting, then we in turn will help you. We can give you a gift that will allow you to ride any horse so well that men will think you a centaur.

We lead the Forest Folk, but the Forest Folk are one with the forest. We are all forest, and so we are all one.

He is a friend of the Forest Folk, for when the Purple Dragons stir from Thunderstone, it is almost always due to him.

We do. It is not far from here - you just need to travel west <StartAction>[The option to travel to the barrows is now enabled to the west]</Start>. We saw a column of Purple Dragons traveling there on our way to the meeting. Edgar Truesilver was with them. He is a friend of ours, a hunter of raiders. If Hawklin sent you to him, you must hurry.
Wandering in Hullack Forest is a dangerous pastime.
It is not wise to pick a fight with the Forest Folk in our own domain. Do you have a reason to be here?
You are an arrogant one. The forest is not forgiving of misplaced confidence.
Hmmm. We think you might be our friend, <FullName>. Maybe there is something you can do for us?
This is the one from Thunderstone, that we have been watching.
Sir Hawklin's messenger? Then perhaps your strange behavior makes more sense. We are called Manthis.
I thought we were looking for a satyr for information, not for a fight.
Why?
You tell us why you seek him, and we shall tell you how to find Manthis.
Good. We are glad you came. Not all in Thunderstone can be trusted like Hawklin. We are called Manthis.
Peace of the Forest on you, <FullName>.
Aye. We will share what we know about these raids. The war made Cormyr forget Hullack Forest for too long. Blight grows here. It needs to be cut away like fungus from a tree.

Hobgoblin bands are loose in the forest. They attack the farms along the edge of the forest, and slay the Forest Folk they find. But these are just random actions to mask a more calculating purpose: they are ransacking all of the ancient barrows. Why, we do not know.
That is the strange part. Some of our folk have seen people from Thunderstone, talking to hobgoblins under the eaves of our forest.
Someone in Thunderstone is hunting the Forest Folk, murdering our families. We don't know who for certain. Can you find a way to stop it?

The raiders come from an old fort which lies deeper in the forest. Polter's Fort it is called. It is an old place and was at peace with the forest, abandoned for centuries. Now someone lives there again, sending out bands to spoil our forest and kill our young.
You must tell Sir Gilbert Hawklin. He is the only one in Thunderstone who cares about us. He will stop these raids.
We are glad. Sir Hawklin will intervene. Tell us, is there anything else you need?
Many raiders already die here in the forest at our hands. Perhaps there is further help we can offer, but first we shall wait to see what Sir Hawklin will do. We are not strong enough to act alone.
We should release the messenger bird immediately to tell Sir Hawklin this information.
We should release the messenger bird immediately to tell Sir Hawklin this information.
At last! Some real news.

Your choice. We are saddened, but we wish you luck. We will meet again, we are sure of it.

Alas, we know nothing more, or we would have acted. We suspect one of the lords since many of them like to hunt; the Wyvernspurs, the Huntsilvers and the Huntcrowns in particular.Maybe it is one of them.

We meet again, as we promised.
Mostly you will face goblins and hobgoblins. They will be easy to kill though their shamans can summon the Undead. There are ballistae on the walls, and you may also find ogres.
Inside, we believe there are vampires sheltering from daylight. We don't know what else is inside, though the fort does not feel right...not peaceful like it once did.

The castle has a square outer wall, with a moat in front and on one side. The main gate is across a drawbridge, but there is also a postern gate on the east side. Both gates have ballistae watching them, two on the main gate, and one on the postern.
Some towers also have archers in them, but if the alarm is not raised, most of the guards will be asleep.
Now we must go. We can hear the whisper of the forest. We are needed.
Goodbye and good luck <FirstName>. We shall not meet again.
I asked you before to find out who hunts the Forest Folk. What can you tell us?
Huntcrown? We thought so, but we hoped not. He is a lord.

These gloves were made by Glauros the centaur from the hair of many of our folk. If you wear them, you will be the master of your horse. Take them with our thanks. This is a bright <quarterday>, <FirstName>, though I came for another reason.
I came to bring you information on Polter's Fort.
What happened?
We tried to get an oath out of him to stop hunting your people, but he pretended he had nothing to do with it!
Why?

Not long ago we had a ball at the castle with many of the nobles from Thunderstone and further afield. At dinner I was sitting next to Lord Marvin Huntcrown. He was going on about hunting and I was only half listening to him, but I remember he was saying how he wished it were legal to hunt unicorns, because he had always wanted a unicorn horn.
Oh! This is dreadful news! It is not long since a unicorn was slain in this forest!
Can you prove it was Huntcrown?
Kathryn Hawklin, you are young and with secrets of your own, but your heart is good. We think you can be believed.
Kathryn Hawklin is young, and with secrets of her own, but her heart is good. If she told you, then we think she can be believed.
Well thanks...I think!
We know Alice Broadhand. She is a dangerous woman and a clever one, but if she told you then it is probably true.
We offer it anyway. It cannot harm you to listen.
We thank you. You did not stop the hunting, but at least now we will watch Lord Huntcrown. One day maybe we will hunt him.
Why not?
Hmmm...yes, though in the forest, the strong survive unless the weak band together. This is nature's way. We will think about it.
One death deserves another. Or are the Forest Folk less than Lord Huntcrown?
We see that you told us in faith ... so he shall live.
We thank you for your help. We offer you information on Polter's Fort as thanks.
We are saddened. We hoped you would find something for us. We cannot wait while we are hunted. We shall have to withdraw deeper into the forest. For this reason, we shall not meet again.
But before we go, we have something for you.
As you wish.

The fort is almost empty; there are raiders all over the forest. Even so, the fort has defenses of its own, including ballistae on the walls, and a drawbridge that can be easily raised. Your best chance of getting into the main fort is to strike quickly and fast, or get in unseen.

Not far ahead is the guardpost, but there may also be scouts around. You need to kill them all, so that none reach the fort with a warning. The hobgoblins at the fort itself often sleep during the <day/night>, relying on this guardpost. You must not let the guards raise the alarm.
That is all we can tell you for now.
Just one then we must leave. Ask it.
There is a gong at the end of the bridge that leads into the castle. Some of the scouts will have orders to run to this gong and ignore you if they see you. You must find a way to kill them first.
I do not want your information, and nor do I trust you.
What can I expect to fight?
Can you tell me the layout of the castle?
Goodbye Manthis.
Wait, one more question.
I am certain that Lord Huntcrown is behind it. I have here a written oath from him swearing to never hunt the Forest Folk.
I'm not interested.
Here you go.
I am certain that Lord Huntcrown is behind it, but I was unable to get any proof.

This module uses a lot of sounds and graphics are at a level that really pushes this engine.  With that said there are a few things you should consider when dealing with lag.
#1 - Check your sound settings.  If they are not set to use HARDWARE acceleration and are instead on SOFTWARE then you can expect lag.   The CPU has to handle mixing all of the sounds and we used a lot of them in designing this module.
#2 - Check your video settings and see if you can reduce some of them.  This may reduce the lag.
#3 - Your video card should have at least 128MB of RAM and preferably should be something in the Geforce 6xxx series or newer.
#4 - If this still does not fix your problems try posting on the premium module technical support forums at http://nwn.bioware.com/ or posting on the DLA forums at http://www.dladventures.net/
